P0001.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit/Open
P0001.plain: The ECU detects an open circuit in the control of fuel volume regulator A (often the metering valve on the high-pressure fuel pump). The actuator does not respond, so rail pressure cannot be controlled accurately.

P0002.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0002.plain: The control signal of fuel volume regulator A is electrically present but the actual rail pressure does not follow the target value within tolerance. Indicates a mechanical or hydraulic issue rather than pure wiring.
causes: High-pressure pump worn or leaking internally

P0003.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit Low
P0003.plain: The ECU sees the control voltage of fuel volume regulator A pulled below the expected range, typically a short to ground or a low-resistance fault in the wiring or coil.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0004.title: Fuel Volume Regulator A Control Circuit High
P0004.plain: The ECU sees the control voltage of fuel volume regulator A above the expected range, typically a short to power or open ground return.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0005.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit/Open
P0005.plain: Open circuit detected at the fuel shutoff valve A solenoid (used on diesels to stop fuel flow at engine-off and as anti-theft). Engine may not start or not stop cleanly.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P0006.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit Low
P0006.plain: Control voltage of fuel shutoff valve A is below the expected range, typically caused by a short to ground or low-resistance fault in the solenoid circuit.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0007.title: Fuel Shutoff Valve A Control Circuit High
P0007.plain: Control voltage of fuel shutoff valve A is above the expected range, typically caused by a short to power or open ground return.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0008.title: Engine Position System Performance Bank 1
P0008.plain: The ECU detects an implausible relationship between crankshaft and camshaft signals on bank 1, indicating timing chain stretch, jumped tooth, or sensor reluctor wear.

P0009.title: Engine Position System Performance Bank 2
P0009.plain: Same fault pattern as P0008 but on bank 2 of a V or boxer engine. Crank/cam correlation outside spec on the second cylinder bank.
causes: Chain jumped one tooth on bank 2

P000A.title: A Camshaft Position Slow Response Bank 1
P000A.plain: The intake camshaft phaser on bank 1 responds too slowly to commanded position changes. Often caused by VVT solenoid sticking, oil aging, or low oil pressure.
causes: Low oil pressure or wrong oil viscosity

P000B.title: B Camshaft Position Slow Response Bank 1
P000B.plain: The exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 1 responds too slowly to commanded position changes. Same root causes as P000A but on the exhaust cam.

P000C.title: A Camshaft Position Slow Response Bank 2
P000C.plain: Intake camshaft phaser on bank 2 responds too slowly. Same fault pattern as P000A on the second cylinder bank.

P000D.title: B Camshaft Position Slow Response Bank 2
P000D.plain: Exhaust camshaft phaser on bank 2 responds too slowly. Same fault pattern as P000B on the second cylinder bank.

P000E.title: Fuel Volume Regulator Control Exceeded Learning Limit
P000E.plain: The ECU's adaptive correction of fuel volume regulator A has reached its learning limit. Indicates a long-term drift between commanded and actual rail pressure that could no longer be compensated.

P000F.title: Fuel System Over Pressure Relief Valve Activated
P000F.plain: The mechanical pressure relief valve on the fuel rail has opened due to overpressure. Indicates a malfunction of the rail pressure regulation that drove pressure beyond the safe limit.

P0010.title: "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 1)
P0010.plain: An electrical fault in the bank 1 intake camshaft position actuator solenoid (variable valve timing). The ECU monitors current and feedback on the oil control valve and sets this code when the circuit is open, shorted, or out of range.
causes: Wiring or connector fault to actuator

P0011.title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced or System Performance (Bank 1)
P0011.plain: The bank 1 intake camshaft is more advanced than commanded, or the actuator does not respond as expected. Often caused by stuck-open oil control valves, sludge in VVT passages, or low oil pressure.
causes: Sludge or debris in VVT oil passages
Low engine oil pressure or wrong oil viscosity

P0012.title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 1)
P0012.plain: The bank 1 intake camshaft remains retarded compared to commanded position. Common causes include a stuck-closed oil control valve, blocked oil passages, or a worn cam phaser.

P0013.title: "B" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 1)
P0013.plain: Electrical fault in the bank 1 exhaust camshaft position actuator solenoid. Same diagnostic principle as P0010 but on the exhaust cam.

P0014.title: "B" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 1)
P0014.plain: Exhaust camshaft position bank 1 over-advanced or system performance — the actual cam phase exceeds the commanded value. Usually caused by a stuck-open oil control valve, low oil pressure, sludged passages, or a worn cam phaser. Confirm with a scan tool live data: command 0° advance and watch actual.

P0015.title: "B" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 1)
P0015.plain: The bank 1 exhaust camshaft remains retarded relative to commanded position. Same root causes as P0012 but on the exhaust cam.

P0016.title: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A)
P0016.plain: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor A): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

P0017.title: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor B)
P0017.plain: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 1 Sensor B): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

P0018.title: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 2 Sensor A)
P0018.plain: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 2 Sensor A): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

P0019.title: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 2 Sensor B)
P0019.plain: Crankshaft Position - Camshaft Position Correlation (Bank 2 Sensor B): the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern. This relates to engine timing; a fault can cause rough running, a no-start, or timing errors.

P001A.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 1
P001A.plain: Open circuit at the camshaft profile actuator (intake, profile A, bank 1). Used by systems with discrete cam-lift levels (e.g. BMW Valvetronic, Honda VTEC, Audi AVS) — the actuator that selects the lift profile cannot be driven.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P001B.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P001B.plain: Low control voltage at the cam profile actuator (intake, profile A, bank 1). Typically a short to ground in the wiring or actuator coil.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P001C.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit High Bank 1
P001C.plain: Excessively high control voltage at the cam profile actuator (intake, profile A, bank 1). Typically a short to power or open ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P001D.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 2
P001D.plain: Open circuit at the cam profile actuator (intake, profile A, bank 2). Same fault as P001A but on bank 2. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P001E.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P001E.plain: Low control voltage at the cam profile actuator (intake, profile A, bank 2). Same fault as P001B on bank 2. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P001F.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit High Bank 2
P001F.plain: Excessively high control voltage at the cam profile actuator (intake, profile A, bank 2). Same fault as P001C on bank 2. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0020.title: "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 2)
P0020.plain: Electrical fault in the bank 2 intake camshaft position actuator. Same diagnostic principle as P0010 but on the second cylinder bank.

P0021.title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 2)
P0021.plain: The bank 2 intake camshaft is more advanced than commanded, or the actuator does not respond as expected. Often caused by stuck-open oil control valves, sludge in VVT passages, or low oil pressure.

P0022.title: "A" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 2)
P0022.plain: The bank 2 intake camshaft remains retarded compared to commanded position. Common causes include a stuck-closed oil control valve, blocked oil passages, or a worn cam phaser.

P0023.title: "B" Camshaft Position Actuator Circuit (Bank 2)
P0023.plain: Electrical fault in the bank 2 exhaust camshaft position actuator. Same diagnostic principle as P0013 but on the second cylinder bank.

P0024.title: "B" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Advanced (Bank 2)
P0024.plain: The bank 2 exhaust camshaft is more advanced than commanded. Same root causes as P0011 but on the exhaust cam.

P0025.title: "B" Camshaft Position - Timing Over-Retarded (Bank 2)
P0025.plain: The bank 2 exhaust camshaft remains retarded relative to commanded position. Same root causes as P0012 but on the exhaust cam.

P0026.title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P0026.plain: The ECU detected that the bank 1 intake valve oil control solenoid does not respond as expected. Common causes are sludge in the oil passages, a sticking solenoid, or low oil pressure that prevents proper VVT phasing on the intake side.
causes: Sludge or debris in oil passages
Low oil pressure or wrong oil viscosity

P0027.title: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
P0027.plain: The ECU detects that the exhaust camshaft oil control valve on bank 1 does not respond to commanded duty cycle within expected limits. Camshaft phase deviates from target during phaser actuation tests.
causes: Oil control valve clogged with sludge
Low oil pressure or wrong oil viscosity

P0028.title: Intake Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P0028.plain: The ECU detected that the bank 2 intake valve oil control solenoid does not respond as expected. Common causes are sludge in the oil passages, a sticking solenoid, or low oil pressure that prevents proper VVT phasing on the intake side.
causes: Sludge or debris in oil passages
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0029.title: Exhaust Valve Control Solenoid Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2
P0029.plain: The ECU detects that the exhaust camshaft oil control valve on bank 2 does not respond to commanded duty cycle within expected limits. Camshaft phase deviates from target during phaser actuation tests.
causes: Oil control valve clogged with sludge
Low oil pressure or wrong oil viscosity

P002A.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 1
P002A.plain: Open circuit at the cam profile actuator on the exhaust cam (profile A, bank 1). Same diagnosis as P001A but for the exhaust profile actuator.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P002B.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P002B.plain: Low control voltage at the exhaust cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 1). Short to ground in wiring or coil.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P002C.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit High Bank 1
P002C.plain: Excessively high control voltage at the exhaust cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 1). Short to power or open ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P002D.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit/Open Bank 2
P002D.plain: Open circuit at the exhaust cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 2). Same as P002A on bank 2. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P002E.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P002E.plain: Low control voltage at the exhaust cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 2). Same as P002B on bank 2. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P002F.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Circuit High Bank 2
P002F.plain: Excessively high control voltage at the exhaust cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 2). Same as P002C on bank 2. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0030.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0030.plain: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 1): the control circuit has an electrical fault. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.
causes: Heater element open or burnt out

P0031.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0031.plain: O2 sensor heater control circuit on bank 1, sensor 1 reports low voltage. Likely shorted to ground or open in the heater control wire. The heater warms the sensor element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Heater control wire shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0032.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0032.plain: O2 sensor heater control circuit on bank 1, sensor 1 reports high voltage. Likely shorted to B+ or open in the heater element itself. The heater warms the sensor element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Heater wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0033.title: Turbocharger Bypass Valve Control Circuit
P0033.plain: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the turbocharger bypass (wastegate) valve control circuit. Voltage or current measured on the solenoid output deviates from expected values during commanded actuation.
causes: Open or shorted wiring to solenoid

P0034.title: Turbocharger Bypass Valve Control Circuit Low
P0034.plain: The bypass valve solenoid control circuit reports a voltage below threshold, indicating a short to ground or open driver. The ECU disables boost control until the fault clears.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0035.title: Turbocharger Bypass Valve Control Circuit High
P0035.plain: The bypass valve solenoid control circuit reports a voltage above threshold, indicating a short to power or open circuit. Boost control is disabled while the fault is active.
causes: Signal wire shorted to battery voltage
Open circuit in wiring or solenoid
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0036.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0036.plain: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2): the control circuit has an electrical fault. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.

P0037.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0037.plain: O2 sensor heater control circuit on bank 1, sensor 2 reports low voltage. Likely shorted to ground or open in the heater control wire. The heater warms the sensor element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0038.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0038.plain: The heater control line for the upstream bank 1 oxygen sensor reads above the expected voltage, typical of a short to supply.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0039.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Control Circuit Range/Performance
P0039.plain: The wastegate or bypass valve A on the turbo/supercharger does not respond mechanically as expected to its control signal. Boost pressure deviates from target.

P003A.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P003A.plain: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Position Exceeded Learning Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.

P003B.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Position Exceeded Learning Limit
P003B.plain: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Position Exceeded Learning Limit: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.

P003C.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1
P003C.plain: The intake cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 1) does not engage when commanded — stays in low-lift profile. Often hydraulic pin sticking or low oil pressure.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P003D.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Stuck On Bank 1
P003D.plain: The intake cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 1) stays engaged when commanded off — stuck in high-lift profile. Idle quality and emissions affected.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P003E.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 2
P003E.plain: The intake cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 2) does not engage when commanded — stays in low-lift profile. Often hydraulic pin sticking or low oil pressure.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P003F.title: A Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Stuck On Bank 2
P003F.plain: The intake cam profile actuator (profile A, bank 2) stays engaged when commanded off — stuck in high-lift profile. Idle quality and emissions affected.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P0040.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 1/Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0040.plain: The pre-cat oxygen sensors of bank 1 and bank 2 appear to be wired the wrong way around — bank 1 reacts when bank 2 should and vice versa. Typically after recent service.

P0041.title: O2 Sensor Signals Swapped Bank 1 Sensor 2/Bank 2 Sensor 2
P0041.plain: The post-cat oxygen sensors of bank 1 and bank 2 appear to be wired the wrong way around — bank 1 reacts when bank 2 should and vice versa. Typically after recent service.

P0042.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Bank 1 Sensor 3
P0042.plain: Generic electrical fault in the heater control of the bank 1, sensor 3 oxygen sensor (typically a third sensor downstream of multi-stage cat or NOx trap).

P0043.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low Bank 1 Sensor 3
P0043.plain: Heater control voltage of the bank 1, sensor 3 oxygen sensor is below the expected range — short to ground or low-resistance fault.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0044.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High Bank 1 Sensor 3
P0044.plain: Heater control voltage of the bank 1, sensor 3 oxygen sensor is above the expected range — short to power or open ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0045.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit/Open
P0045.plain: Open circuit at the boost control solenoid/actuator A. The ECU cannot drive the wastegate or VGT vanes.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P0046.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit Range/Performance
P0046.plain: Boost control actuator A is electrically active but boost pressure deviates from target. Mechanical or hydraulic limitation.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0047.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit Low
P0047.plain: Boost control circuit A voltage below expected range — short to ground or low-resistance fault in solenoid wiring.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0048.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit High
P0048.plain: Boost control circuit A voltage above expected range — short to power or open ground in solenoid wiring.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0049.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger A Turbine Overspeed
P0049.plain: The turbocharger A turbine speed exceeded its safe limit. Risk of bearing damage and shaft fracture. Often caused by a stuck-closed wastegate or boost control fault.

P004A.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Circuit/Open
P004A.plain: Open circuit at boost control solenoid B (twin-turbo or two-stage system). Same diagnosis as P0045 on actuator B.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P004B.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Circuit Range/Performance
P004B.plain: Boost control B mechanical/hydraulic deviation from target. Same as P0046 on actuator B. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P004C.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Circuit Low
P004C.plain: Boost control B circuit voltage below expected range. Same as P0047 on actuator B. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P004D.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Circuit High
P004D.plain: Boost control B circuit voltage above expected range. Same as P0048 on actuator B. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P004E.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P004E.plain: Intermittent dropouts or noise on boost control A circuit. Loose connector, partial wiring break, or solenoid degrading.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P004F.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P004F.plain: Same intermittent fault pattern as P004E on boost control B. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0050.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P0050.plain: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 1): the control circuit has an electrical fault. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.

P0051.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P0051.plain: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 1): the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0052.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P0052.plain: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 1): the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0053.title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 1 Sensor 1
P0053.plain: The heater resistance of the bank 1, sensor 1 oxygen sensor is outside its specified range. Sensor heater aging or short between heater and signal.

P0054.title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 1 Sensor 2
P0054.plain: The heater resistance of the bank 1, sensor 2 oxygen sensor is outside its specified range. Sensor heater aging or short between heater and signal.

P0055.title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 1 Sensor 3
P0055.plain: The heater resistance of the bank 1, sensor 3 oxygen sensor is outside its specified range. Sensor heater aging or short between heater and signal.

P0056.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P0056.plain: HO2S Heater Control Circuit (Bank 2 Sensor 2): the control circuit has an electrical fault. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.

P0057.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P0057.plain: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low (Bank 2 Sensor 2): the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0058.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P0058.plain: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High (Bank 2 Sensor 2): the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. The heater brings the oxygen sensor to operating temperature for closed-loop fuel control.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0059.title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 2 Sensor 1
P0059.plain: Heater resistance out of range on bank 2 sensor 1 (pre-cat). Same diagnostic as P0053 on the second bank.

P005A.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 1
P005A.plain: Exhaust cam profile actuator A on bank 1 stuck disengaged. Same fault pattern as P003C but on the exhaust cam. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P005B.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Stuck On Bank 1
P005B.plain: Exhaust cam profile actuator A on bank 1 stuck engaged. Same fault pattern as P003D on the exhaust cam. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P005C.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Performance/Stuck Off Bank 2
P005C.plain: Exhaust cam profile actuator A on bank 2 stuck disengaged. Same fault pattern as P003C but on the exhaust cam. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P005D.title: B Camshaft Profile Actuator A Control Stuck On Bank 2
P005D.plain: Exhaust cam profile actuator A on bank 2 stuck engaged. Same fault pattern as P003D on the exhaust cam. The cam phaser actuator adjusts intake/exhaust timing under load — a stuck or slow phaser kills mid-rpm torque and can throw correlation codes between cam and crank.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P005E.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P005E.plain: Supply voltage feeding boost control actuator B is below the expected range. Likely fuse, supply wiring or relay fault.
causes: Supply fuse blown or relay failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P005F.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control B Supply Voltage Circuit High
P005F.plain: Supply voltage feeding boost control actuator B is above the expected range. Likely charging system overvoltage or wiring shorted to a higher potential.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0060.title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 2 Sensor 2
P0060.plain: Heater resistance out of range on bank 2 sensor 2 (post-cat). Same diagnostic as P0053 on second bank, post-cat.

P0061.title: HO2S Heater Resistance Bank 2 Sensor 3
P0061.plain: Heater resistance out of range on bank 2 sensor 3. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

P0062.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Bank 2 Sensor 3
P0062.plain: Generic electrical fault in the heater control of bank 2 sensor 3. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

P0063.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Low Bank 2 Sensor 3
P0063.plain: Heater control voltage of bank 2 sensor 3 below the expected range. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0064.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit High Bank 2 Sensor 3
P0064.plain: Heater control voltage of bank 2 sensor 3 above the expected range. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0065.title: Air Assisted Injector Control Range/Performance
P0065.plain: The air-assist injector control system (used on some lean-burn or direct-injection engines to atomize fuel with air) shows a performance deviation from the expected behavior.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0066.title: Air Assisted Injector Control Circuit Low
P0066.plain: Control voltage of the air-assist injector valve is below the expected range — short to ground or low-resistance fault.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0067.title: Air Assisted Injector Control Circuit High
P0067.plain: Control voltage of the air-assist injector valve is above the expected range — short to power or open ground. A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.

P0068.title: MAP/MAF - Throttle Position Correlation
P0068.plain: The ECU detects implausibility between throttle position and the airflow or intake manifold pressure measured. At a given throttle angle the air mass deviates beyond rationality limits.

P0069.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure - Barometric Pressure Correlation
P0069.plain: At engine cranking or key-on the intake manifold pressure should equal barometric pressure within tolerance. The ECU detects a deviation indicating sensor drift or vacuum line issues.
causes: Vacuum hose to MAP sensor leaking

P006A.title: MAP - Mass or Volume Air Flow Correlation Bank 1
P006A.plain: The expected relationship between manifold absolute pressure (MAP) and mass airflow (MAF) on bank 1 is violated. One of the two sensors is reading incorrectly.

P006B.title: MAP - Exhaust Pressure Correlation
P006B.plain: The relationship between manifold absolute pressure and exhaust back pressure is implausible. One of the two pressure sensors is faulty or there is a major leak in either path.

P006C.title: MAP - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Correlation
P006C.plain: The relationship between manifold absolute pressure and turbocharger inlet pressure is implausible. Indicates a leak between turbo inlet and intake manifold or a sensor fault.
causes: Charge pipe leak between turbo and intake

P006D.title: Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Correlation Bank 1
P006D.plain: The relationship between barometric pressure and turbo inlet pressure (bank 1) is implausible — at engine off the two should match. Indicates an inlet sensor or barometric sensor fault.

P006E.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P006E.plain: Supply voltage to boost control actuator A below expected range. Same as P005E but on actuator A. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Supply fuse blown or relay failed
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P006F.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control A Supply Voltage Circuit High

P0071.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit A Range/Performance
P0071.plain: The ambient air temperature reading is electrically valid but implausible compared to other temperature sources (intake air temp, coolant at cold start).
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0072.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit A Low
P0072.plain: Ambient air temperature sensor A signal voltage below the expected range — typically a short to ground.

P0073.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit A High

P0074.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit A Intermittent/Erratic

P0087.title: Fuel Rail/System Pressure Too Low
P0087.plain: The ECU detects fuel rail pressure below the desired setpoint despite maximum pump and metering valve commands. Common in direct injection diesel and gasoline systems where high-pressure pump or rail pressure regulator fails.

P0088.title: Fuel Rail/System Pressure Too High
P0088.plain: The ECU detects fuel rail pressure above the desired setpoint and cannot reduce it through pressure regulator commands. Risk of injector damage and rail seal failure if not addressed.

P0089.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator 1 Performance
P0089.plain: The ECU detects that fuel rail pressure does not respond to commanded changes of the pressure regulator within expected dynamics. Indicates a sluggish or partially failed regulator.

P008A.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Pressure - Too Low
P008A.plain: The low-pressure (lift pump) fuel pressure is below the expected value. Insufficient supply to the high-pressure pump leads to power loss and possible HP pump cavitation.
causes: Leak or air ingress in low-pressure line

P008B.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Pressure - Too High
P008B.plain: The low-pressure fuel pressure is above the expected value. Often caused by a stuck-closed fuel return valve or a faulty pressure regulator.

P008C.title: Fuel Cooler Pump Control Circuit/Open
P008C.plain: Open circuit at the fuel cooler pump control. The pump that circulates fuel through a cooler (used on diesels and some hot-fuel applications) cannot be driven.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P008D.title: Fuel Cooler Pump Control Circuit Low
P008D.plain: Control voltage of the fuel cooler pump is below the expected range — short to ground or low-resistance fault.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P008E.title: Fuel Cooler Pump Control Circuit High
P008E.plain: Control voltage of the fuel cooler pump is above the expected range — short to power or open ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P008F.title: Engine Coolant Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation

P0090.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Control Circuit/Open
P0090.plain: Open circuit at fuel pressure regulator A. The actuator that controls rail pressure cannot be driven.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P0091.title: Fuel Pressure Regulator A Control Circuit Low

P0093.title: Fuel System Leak Detected - Large Leak
P0093.plain: The ECU detected a large leak in the fuel system. Rail pressure cannot be maintained, often visible as fuel odor or visible drips.
causes: Fuel line cracked or fitting loose

P0094.title: Fuel System Leak Detected - Small Leak
P0094.plain: A small fuel system leak detected by long-term pressure drop pattern. Often a slowly weeping injector or hairline crack in a fitting.

P0095.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 2 Circuit Bank 1

P009A.title: Intake Air Temperature/Ambient Air Temperature Correlation

P009F.title: Fuel Pressure Relief Control Stuck On
P009F.plain: Pressure relief solenoid stays open when not commanded — rail pressure cannot build up properly.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P00B2.plain: Radiator coolant sensor reading implausible compared to engine coolant or expected behavior. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.

P00B5.title: Radiator Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic

P00B6.title: Radiator Coolant Temperature/Engine Coolant Temperature Correlation
P00B6.plain: Difference between radiator outlet and engine coolant temperatures is implausible — typically indicates a stuck thermostat.

P00B7.title: Engine Coolant Flow Low/Performance
P00B7.plain: Coolant flow through the engine is below the expected level. Risk of overheating.
causes: Water pump impeller broken or worn

P00B8.title: MAP - Mass or Volume Air Flow Correlation Bank 2
P00B8.plain: The expected relationship between manifold absolute pressure (MAP) and mass airflow (MAF) on bank 2 is violated. One of the two sensors is reading incorrectly.

P00B9.title: Low Pressure Fuel System Pressure - Too Low. Low Ambient Temperature
P00B9.plain: Low-pressure fuel circuit pressure below target under cold ambient conditions. Often diesel waxing or gelled fuel filter.

P00BA.title: Low Fuel Pressure - Forced Limited Power
P00BA.plain: Fuel pressure too low — ECU has activated forced power reduction (limp mode) to protect the fuel system.

P00BB.title: Fuel Injector Insufficient Flow - Forced Limited Power
P00BB.plain: One or more injectors deliver less fuel than commanded — ECU has activated forced power reduction. A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.

P00BC.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow A Circuit Range/Performance - Air Flow Too Low
P00BC.plain: Mass or Volume Air Flow A Circuit Range/Performance - Air Flow Too Low: the signal is implausible or outside the valid range.

P00BD.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow A Circuit Range/Performance - Air Flow Too High

P00BF.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow B Circuit Range/Performance - Air Flow Too High

P00C0.plain: Generic electrical fault on bypass valve B control. Same family as P0039 on actuator B. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

P00C4.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B - Mechanical
P00C4.plain: Mechanical fault detected at bypass valve B — broken linkage, jammed valve, or seized actuator rod. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

P00C6.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Too Low - Engine Cranking Bank 1
