P00CE.title: Intake Air Temperature Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 1
P00CE.plain: Multiple intake air temperature sensors on bank 1 disagree beyond plausible limits. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).

P00CF.title: Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor A Correlation
P00CF.plain: Barometric pressure and boost sensor A readings disagree at engine off — they should match without boost.

P00D0.title: Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Sensor B Correlation
P00D0.plain: Barometric pressure and boost sensor B readings disagree at engine off — they should match without boost.

P00D1.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 1
P00D1.plain: Heater control of bank 1 sensor 1 is electrically OK but does not heat the sensor as expected — element aged or wiring resistance high.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P00D2.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1 Sensor 2
P00D2.plain: Heater control of bank 1 sensor 2 is electrically OK but does not heat the sensor as expected — element aged or wiring resistance high.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P00D3.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 1
P00D3.plain: Heater control of bank 2 sensor 1 is electrically OK but does not heat the sensor as expected — element aged or wiring resistance high.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P00D4.title: HO2S Heater Control Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2 Sensor 2
P00D4.plain: Heater control of bank 2 sensor 2 is electrically OK but does not heat the sensor as expected — element aged or wiring resistance high.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P00D5.title: HO2S Sensor Correlation Bank 1 Sensor 1/Bank 1 Sensor 2
P00D5.plain: Pre- and post-cat oxygen sensors on bank 1 do not correlate as expected — typical sign of catalyst inefficiency or one failed sensor.

P00D6.title: HO2S Sensor Correlation Bank 2 Sensor 1/Bank 2 Sensor 2
P00D6.plain: Pre- and post-cat oxygen sensors on bank 2 do not correlate as expected — typical sign of catalyst inefficiency or one failed sensor.

P00D7.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Temperature Too High
P00D7.plain: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve A Temperature Too High: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.
causes: Cooling system not adequately removing heat

P00D8.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B Temperature Too High
P00D8.plain: Turbocharger/Supercharger Bypass Valve B Temperature Too High: the component is overheating, typically from extended load or slip. This affects turbo/supercharger boost-pressure control.

P00D9.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit B
P00D9.plain: Generic electrical fault on ambient air temperature sensor B (second sensor for redundancy or second measurement location).

P00DA.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit B Range/Performance
P00DA.plain: Ambient air temperature sensor B reading implausible compared to other sources.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P00DB.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit B Low
P00DB.plain: Ambient air temp sensor B signal voltage below expected range.

P00DC.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit B High
P00DC.plain: Ambient air temp sensor B signal voltage above expected range.

P00DD.title: Ambient Air Temperature Sensor Circuit B Intermittent/Erratic
P00DD.plain: Intermittent signal from ambient air temp sensor B.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P00DE.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P00DE.plain: Generic electrical fault at the charge air cooler coolant temperature sensor A (water-cooled CAC system).

P00DF.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P00DF.plain: CAC coolant temp sensor A reading implausible. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P00E0.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P00E0.plain: CAC coolant temp sensor A signal voltage below expected range. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P00E1.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P00E1.plain: CAC coolant temp sensor A signal voltage above expected range. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P00E2.title: Charge Air Cooler Coolant Temperature Sensor A Intermittent/Erratic
P00E2.plain: Intermittent signal from CAC coolant temp sensor A. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P00E3.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Exhaust Bypass Valve A Stuck Open
P00E3.plain: The exhaust heat exchanger bypass valve A is stuck open. Engine warms up too slowly because exhaust does not heat the heat exchanger.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P00E4.title: Exhaust Heat Exchanger Exhaust Bypass Valve A Stuck Closed
P00E4.plain: The exhaust heat exchanger bypass valve A is stuck closed. Risk of overheating because exhaust always passes through the heat exchanger.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P00E5.title: Intake Air Temperature/Fuel Temperature Correlation
P00E5.plain: Intake air and fuel temperature readings are inconsistent — at long soak both should match ambient. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).

P00E6.title: Intake Air Pressure Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 2
P00E6.plain: Multiple intake air pressure sensors on bank 2 disagree with each other beyond the plausible deviation. One has drifted.

P00E7.title: Intake Air Temperature Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation Bank 2
P00E7.plain: Multiple intake air temperature sensors on bank 2 disagree beyond plausible limits. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).

P00E8.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Bank 1
P00E8.plain: Generic electrical fault on intake air temperature sensor 3 (third measurement location, e.g. in throttle or after intercooler) on bank 1.

P00E9.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Range/Performance Bank 1
P00E9.plain: IAT sensor 3 reading on bank 1 implausible. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P00EA.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Low Bank 1
P00EA.plain: IAT sensor 3 bank 1 signal voltage below expected range. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P00EB.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit High Bank 1
P00EB.plain: IAT sensor 3 bank 1 signal voltage above expected range. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P00EC.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 1
P00EC.plain: Intermittent signal from IAT sensor 3 on bank 1. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P00ED.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Bank 2
P00ED.plain: Generic electrical fault on intake air temperature sensor 3 (third measurement location, e.g. in throttle or after intercooler) on bank 2.

P00EE.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Range/Performance Bank 2
P00EE.plain: IAT sensor 3 reading on bank 2 implausible. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P00EF.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Low Bank 2
P00EF.plain: IAT sensor 3 bank 2 signal voltage below expected range. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P00F0.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit High Bank 2
P00F0.plain: IAT sensor 3 bank 2 signal voltage above expected range. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P00F1.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor 3 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic Bank 2
P00F1.plain: Intermittent signal from IAT sensor 3 on bank 2. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P00F2.title: Humidity Sensor Circuit/Open
P00F2.plain: Open circuit at the humidity sensor (used by ECU for combustion correction, especially on direct-injection engines).
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P00F3.title: Humidity Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P00F3.plain: Humidity sensor reading implausible. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P00F4.title: Humidity Sensor Circuit Low
P00F4.plain: Humidity sensor signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P00F5.title: Humidity Sensor Circuit High
P00F5.plain: Humidity sensor signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P00F6.title: Humidity Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P00F6.plain: Intermittent signal from humidity sensor. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P00F7.title: Barometric Pressure - Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Correlation Bank 2
P00F7.plain: The relationship between barometric pressure and turbo inlet pressure (bank 2) is implausible — at engine off the two should match. Indicates an inlet sensor or barometric sensor fault.

P00F8.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P00F8.plain: Generic electrical fault on turbocharger outlet pressure sensor A (post-compressor pressure measurement).

P00F9.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Range/Performance
P00F9.plain: Turbo outlet pressure sensor A reading implausible. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P00FA.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P00FA.plain: Turbo outlet pressure sensor A signal voltage below expected range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P00FB.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P00FB.plain: Turbo outlet pressure sensor A signal voltage above expected range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P00FC.title: Turbocharger Outlet Pressure Sensor A Intermittent/Erratic
P00FC.plain: Intermittent signal from turbo outlet pressure sensor A. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P00FD.title: Battery B State of Charge Performance
P00FD.plain: State of charge of battery B (typically auxiliary or hybrid battery) shows performance fault — does not behave according to charging model.

P00FE.title: EVAP System Tank Vapor Line Restricted/Blocked
P00FE.plain: The EVAP tank vapor line is restricted or blocked. Tank pressure cannot equalize properly. The evaporative system captures fuel vapor from the tank and purges it into intake; leaks or stuck purge valves leak hydrocarbons and cause emissions failures.

P00FF.title: Body Control Module Requested MIL Illumination
P00FF.plain: The Body Control Module (BCM) sent a request to the engine ECU to illuminate the MIL — actual fault is in a body system; this is a forwarded request, not a powertrain fault.
causes: Underlying BCM fault — read BCM codes

P0100.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Malfunction
P0100.plain: The ECU detects a general electrical malfunction in the mass air flow (MAF) sensor circuit. The signal is missing, out of plausible range, or the wiring shows continuity issues. Used as a generic fault when no more specific MAF code applies.

P0101.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Range/Performance
P0101.plain: The mass air flow (MAF) sensor signal is outside the expected range or does not track engine load plausibly. The ECU compares MAF readings against load calculated from RPM, throttle position and intake pressure; persistent disagreement triggers this code.

P0102.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Low Input
P0102.plain: The MAF sensor reports an air flow value below the plausible minimum for current engine speed and load. The ECU substitutes a calculated load value while the fault is active.

P0103.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit High Input
P0103.plain: The MAF sensor reports an air flow value above the plausible maximum for current engine speed and load. Often indicates a sensor that is failing in a way that produces excess output, or a short to supply voltage in the signal path.
causes: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0104.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Circuit Intermittent
P0104.plain: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts or noise on the mass air flow (MAF) sensor circuit. The fault is not constantly present, suggesting a loose connection, intermittent wiring break, or a failing sensor under specific conditions (vibration, temperature).

P0105.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure / Barometric Pressure Circuit Malfunction
P0105.plain: The ECU detects a general electrical malfunction in the manifold absolute pressure (MAP) or barometric pressure sensor circuit. Signal missing, implausible, or wiring broken. Generic fault when no more specific MAP code applies.
causes: Vacuum hose to MAP sensor cracked or disconnected

P0106.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
P0106.plain: The manifold absolute pressure (MAP) sensor signal is implausible relative to throttle position and engine speed. The ECU expects MAP to rise with throttle opening and fall under deceleration; deviation triggers the code.
causes: Vacuum hose to MAP sensor cracked or detached

P0107.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Low Input
P0107.plain: The MAP sensor reports a pressure below the lower threshold the ECU expects at any engine state. Typically indicates a hard electrical fault rather than a slow drift.

P0108.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor High Input
P0108.plain: The MAP sensor reports a pressure above the upper threshold the ECU expects in any engine state. Typically caused by a short in the signal circuit or a sensor that has failed producing a fixed high output.
causes: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage

P0109.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure / Barometric Pressure Circuit Intermittent
P0109.plain: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts on the MAP/BARO sensor circuit. Fault is not constantly present — typically caused by loose connectors, chafed wiring, or a sensor failing under thermal load.

P010A.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit
P010A.plain: Generic electrical fault on MAF sensor B (second sensor for redundancy or twin-intake systems).

P010B.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P010B.plain: MAF sensor B reading implausible. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P010C.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit Low
P010C.plain: MAF B signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P010D.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit High
P010D.plain: MAF B signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P010E.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P010E.plain: Intermittent signal from MAF sensor B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P010F.title: Mass or Volume Air Flow Sensor A/B Correlation
P010F.plain: MAF sensor A and B disagree beyond plausible deviation. One is reading incorrectly.

P0110.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0110.plain: The ECU detects a general electrical fault in the intake air temperature (IAT) sensor circuit. Signal absent, shorted or out of plausible range. Generic catch-all when no more specific IAT code (low/high/range) is set.

P0111.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
P0111.plain: The intake air temperature (IAT) sensor reading does not change plausibly with engine warm-up or after driving begins. Many vehicles share the IAT into the MAF housing; on those, MAF replacement also replaces IAT.
causes: Sensor element coated with oil or dirt
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0112.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Low Input
P0112.plain: The IAT signal voltage is below threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly hot intake (low NTC resistance). Usually a wiring short to ground or a failed sensor.

P0113.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor High Input
P0113.plain: The IAT signal voltage is above threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly cold intake (open-circuit-like behaviour). Usually open wiring or a sensor that has failed open.
causes: Open circuit in sensor or wiring

P0114.title: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Intermittent
P0114.plain: The IAT signal shows intermittent dropouts or jumps that fall outside slope expectations but do not stay above or below threshold long enough to trigger P0112/P0113. Usually a wiring or connector issue.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0115.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0115.plain: A general fault has been detected in the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor circuit. The ECU uses ECT for fuel enrichment during cold start, fan control, and closed-loop entry timing.

P0116.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
P0116.plain: The coolant temperature sensor reading does not change plausibly during warm-up, or its value disagrees with the intake air temperature when the engine has been off long enough that they should match. Often caused by a sensor that reports near a fixed value despite engine warm-up.
causes: Thermostat stuck open (engine never reaches operating temperature)
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0117.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Low Input
P0117.plain: The ECT signal voltage is below threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly hot coolant temperature (typical NTC sensor characteristic — low resistance at high temperature).

P0118.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor High Input
P0118.plain: The ECT signal voltage is above threshold, which the ECU interprets as an implausibly cold temperature (open-circuit-like behaviour). When this code is active, the ECU runs a default cold-start enrichment that wastes fuel and may cause black smoke.
causes: Open circuit in sensor or wiring

P0119.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0119.plain: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts on the engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensor circuit. Fault not constantly present, typically due to loose connector, chafed wiring or a sensor failing thermally.
causes: Wiring chafed near hot engine parts

P011A.title: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation
P011A.plain: ECT sensors 1 and 2 readings disagree beyond plausible limits — typically near startup both should match within tolerance.

P011B.title: Engine Coolant Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation
P011B.plain: ECT and IAT readings disagree at long soak (engine off for hours) when both should match ambient. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).

P011C.title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation Bank 1
P011C.plain: CAC temperature and IAT on bank 1 disagree at long soak. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).

P011D.title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature/Intake Air Temperature Correlation Bank 2
P011D.plain: CAC temperature and IAT on bank 2 disagree at long soak. The intake air temperature sensor feeds the ECM's density calculation — a drifted reading miscalculates fuel mass and pushes mixture lean (cold reading) or rich (hot reading).

P011E.title: Engine Coolant Temperature 1 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation
P011E.plain: Engine Coolant Temperature 1 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation: the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern.

P011F.title: Engine Coolant Temperature 2 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation
P011F.plain: Engine Coolant Temperature 2 / Ambient Air Temperature Correlation: the value does not correlate with the related sensor or expected pattern.

P0120.title: Throttle Position Sensor / Switch A Circuit Malfunction
P0120.plain: The ECU detects a general electrical fault on the throttle position sensor/switch A circuit. Signal missing, implausible, or wiring broken. Generic catch-all when no more specific TPS-A code applies.
causes: TPS worn or failed (dead spot in resistive track)
TPS mechanically misaligned to throttle shaft

P0121.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Range/Performance
P0121.plain: The throttle position sensor (TPS) signal does not match the expected range for the commanded pedal position. On drive-by-wire vehicles, two redundant sensors are compared; a divergence between them or implausible motion triggers this code.
causes: TPS contact track worn (older potentiometer-type sensors)

P0122.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Low Input
P0122.plain: The TPS signal voltage is below the lower acceptable threshold. The ECU usually enters limp-home mode and limits engine torque while the fault is active.

P0123.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" High Input
P0123.plain: The TPS signal voltage exceeds the upper acceptable threshold. As with P0122, limp-home mode is typical until the fault clears.
causes: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage

P0124.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Circuit Intermittent
P0124.plain: The TPS signal shows intermittent dropouts that do not stay outside threshold long enough to trigger P0122/P0123. Drive-by-wire systems are sensitive to this and may briefly enter limp-home mode each time.
causes: Sensor track worn at one spot (older potentiometer-type)
Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0125.title: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Closed Loop Fuel Control
P0125.plain: The engine has run long enough that closed-loop fuel control should be active, but the coolant temperature has not risen high enough. Often caused by a stuck-open thermostat or a failed coolant temperature sensor.

P0126.title: Insufficient Coolant Temperature for Stable Operation
P0126.plain: Coolant temperature stays below the value expected for stable engine operation. Almost always points to a thermostat stuck open or a sensor reading lower than the actual engine temperature.

P0127.title: Intake Air Temperature Too High
P0127.plain: Intake air temperature exceeds the safe maximum. Risk of preignition or knock; ECU may reduce power.

P0128.title: Coolant Thermostat Below Regulating Temperature
P0128.plain: The engine has been running long enough to reach operating temperature, but coolant temperature stayed below the thermostat's regulating value. Almost always caused by a thermostat stuck open. Costs fuel economy and increases cold-engine emissions.

P0129.title: Barometric Pressure Too Low
P0129.plain: Barometric pressure reading below the plausible minimum. Either operating at extreme altitude or sensor fault.

P012A.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit
P012A.plain: Generic electrical fault on turbo/supercharger inlet pressure sensor A. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.

P012B.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P012B.plain: Turbo inlet pressure sensor A reading implausible. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P012C.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Low
P012C.plain: Turbo inlet pressure sensor A signal voltage below expected range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P012D.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit High
P012D.plain: Turbo inlet pressure sensor A signal voltage above expected range. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P012E.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Inlet Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P012E.plain: Intermittent signal from turbo inlet pressure sensor A. Boost control tracks commanded vs. actual manifold pressure; persistent deviation means wastegate, vanes, hose or actuator are not delivering the requested pressure.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P012F.title: Engine Coolant Temperature / Engine Oil Temperature Correlation
P012F.plain: Engine coolant and oil temperature readings disagree beyond plausible limits. The engine coolant temperature sensor feeds warm-up enrichment, fan control and closed-loop entry — a stuck-cold reading keeps the engine in open loop and rich forever.

P0130.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P0130.plain: The upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports an implausible signal — typically stuck mid-range, no switching between rich and lean, or no signal at all. Closed-loop fuel control cannot run while this fault is active.

P0131.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P0131.plain: The upstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a low voltage, indicating the ECU sees a continuously lean exhaust on bank 1 — or the sensor signal path is shorted to ground.
causes: Exhaust leak upstream of the sensor
Genuine lean running (vacuum leak, low fuel pressure)

P0132.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P0132.plain: The upstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a high voltage, indicating either a continuously rich exhaust on bank 1 or a short to supply voltage in the signal circuit.
causes: Genuine rich running (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Sensor poisoned by silicone or coolant

P0133.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P0133.plain: The upstream oxygen sensor switches between rich and lean too slowly. Aged sensors lose response speed before they fail outright; this code typically appears before P0130/P0131/P0132.

P0134.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P0134.plain: The ECU detects that the upstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 shows no switching activity or responds too slowly to changing exhaust gas composition. Often the sensor is aged, contaminated by silicone or fuel additives, or the heater circuit is degraded.
causes: Sensor aged or poisoned (silicone, lead, coolant)
Exhaust leak upstream of sensor diluting reading

P0135.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
P0135.plain: The heating element inside the upstream oxygen sensor draws no current, draws too much current, or is open-circuit. The heater brings the sensor to operating temperature so closed-loop control can start within seconds rather than minutes.

P0136.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P0136.plain: A general fault has been detected in the downstream (post-catalyst) oxygen sensor on bank 1. The downstream sensor monitors catalyst efficiency rather than fuel mixture; with no signal, the catalyst monitor cannot run.

P0137.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P0137.plain: The downstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a low voltage. Either the catalyst is letting unburned oxygen through (sensor sees lean), the sensor itself is shorted to ground, or the catalyst is so degraded that the downstream signal mirrors a lean upstream condition.
causes: Exhaust leak between catalyst and downstream sensor

P0138.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P0138.plain: The downstream oxygen sensor signal is fixed at a high voltage, indicating either a continuously rich downstream reading (less common, since post-cat exhaust should be more stable) or a short to supply voltage in the signal circuit.
causes: Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0139.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0139.plain: The ECU detects that the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 reports an abnormally high voltage signal, suggesting a persistently rich exhaust condition past the catalyst, a shorted sensor, or wiring shorted to a voltage source.
causes: Engine running rich (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)
Sensor signal wire shorted to voltage

P013A.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 2
P013A.plain: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean. Sensor aging or contamination.

P013B.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 2
P013B.plain: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P013C.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 2
P013C.plain: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean. Sensor aging or contamination.

P013D.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 2
P013D.plain: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P013E.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 2
P013E.plain: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P013F.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 2
P013F.plain: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P0140.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0140.plain: The ECU detects no switching or excessively slow response from the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1. Typical for an aged or poisoned sensor; downstream sensors should show a relatively flat signal but must respond to fueling changes during diagnostic monitor runs.
causes: Catalytic converter so degraded that downstream signal mirrors upstream

P0141.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 2)
P0141.plain: The heating element inside the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1 is open-circuit, drawing no current, or drawing too much. Without heater, the sensor takes much longer to reach operating temperature, delaying catalyst diagnosis.

P0142.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P0142.plain: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the downstream oxygen sensor on bank 1. The heater current is out of range, suggesting an open or shorted heater element, blown fuse or wiring fault.

P0143.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P0143.plain: The ECU detects a general electrical fault on the third oxygen sensor in the bank 1 exhaust path (typically located after a second catalyst on diesel or large engines with multi-cat exhausts).

P0144.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P0144.plain: The ECU detects an abnormally low voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 1. Indicates persistently lean exhaust, an open sensor or wiring shorted to ground.
causes: Lean exhaust (vacuum leak, low fuel pressure)

P0145.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P0145.plain: The ECU detects an abnormally high voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 1. Indicates persistently rich exhaust, a shorted sensor or wiring shorted to a voltage source.
causes: Rich exhaust (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)

P0146.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P0146.plain: The ECU detects no switching activity or too slow a response from the third O2 sensor on bank 1. Typical for aged or poisoned sensor.

P0147.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1 Sensor 3)
P0147.plain: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the third O2 sensor on bank 1. Heater current out of range, indicating open/shorted heater element, blown fuse or wiring fault.

P0148.title: Fuel Delivery Error
P0148.plain: Fuel quantity actually delivered does not match the commanded value over a long observation window. Mechanical issue in the fuel system.

P0149.title: Fuel Timing Error
P0149.plain: Injection timing deviates from target. Often caused by chain wear, sensor offset, or injector response drift.

P014A.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 2
P014A.plain: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P014B.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 2
P014B.plain: Post-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P014C.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 1
P014C.plain: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P014D.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 1
P014D.plain: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P014E.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 1
P014E.plain: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P014F.title: O2 Sensor Slow Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 1
P014F.plain: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 responds too slowly when mixture transitions from lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P0150.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P0150.plain: Same condition as P0130 but on bank 2 of a multi-bank engine. Closed-loop fuel control on bank 2 is disabled while this fault is active.

P0151.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P0151.plain: Same condition as P0131 but on bank 2. The upstream sensor sees a continuously lean exhaust on bank 2 or has a signal short to ground.
causes: Exhaust leak upstream of the sensor
Bank 2 running lean (vacuum leak, fuel pressure)
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0152.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P0152.plain: Same condition as P0132 but on bank 2. The upstream sensor reports a continuously rich condition or has a short to supply voltage.
causes: Bank 2 running rich (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0153.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P0153.plain: The ECU detects an abnormally high voltage from the upstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates persistently rich exhaust, shorted sensor or wiring shorted to voltage.
causes: Bank 2 running rich (leaking injector, high fuel pressure)

P0154.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P0154.plain: The ECU detects no switching activity or too slow a response from the upstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Typically aged or poisoned sensor, weak heater, or upstream exhaust leak.

P0155.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 1)
P0155.plain: Same condition as P0135 but on the upstream sensor of bank 2. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

P0156.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
P0156.plain: Same condition as P0136 but on the downstream sensor of bank 2. The catalyst efficiency monitor for bank 2 cannot run while this fault is active.

P0157.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P0157.plain: The ECU detects abnormally low voltage from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates persistently lean exhaust past the catalyst, open sensor or wiring shorted to ground.

P0158.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P0158.plain: The ECU detects abnormally low voltage from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2 (alternate definition mapping in some manufacturers' interpretation). Indicates persistent lean reading, open sensor or wiring shorted to ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0159.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P0159.plain: The ECU detects an abnormally high voltage from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates persistently rich exhaust past the cat, shorted sensor or wiring shorted to voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P015A.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 1
P015A.plain: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P015B.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 1
P015B.plain: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 1 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P015C.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 1
P015C.plain: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches rich to lean. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P015D.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 1
P015D.plain: Pre-cat O2 sensor on bank 2 reacts only after delay when mixture switches lean to rich. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P015E.title: Excessive Time to Enter Closed Loop Fuel Timing Control
P015E.plain: ECU took longer than allowed to enter closed-loop control of fuel injection timing. Often slow sensor warm-up.

P015F.title: Excessive Time to Enter Closed Loop Cylinder Balance Control
P015F.plain: ECU took longer than allowed to enter closed-loop cylinder balance control.

P0160.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P0160.plain: The ECU detects no switching or too slow a response from the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Often aged or poisoned sensor; downstream sensors usually flat but must respond on diagnostic monitor runs.

P0161.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2, Sensor 2)
P0161.plain: Same condition as P0141 but on the downstream sensor of bank 2. The sensor heater warms the element to operating temperature (~600 °C); without it the lambda sensor stays inactive in closed loop and the ECM cannot trim mixture.

P0162.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P0162.plain: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the downstream O2 sensor on bank 2. Heater current out of range — open or shorted heater element, blown fuse, or wiring fault.

P0163.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P0163.plain: The ECU detects a general electrical fault on the third O2 sensor in the bank 2 exhaust path (typically post-second-cat in multi-cat exhausts).

P0164.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P0164.plain: The ECU detects abnormally low voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates lean exhaust, open sensor or wiring shorted to ground.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0165.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P0165.plain: The ECU detects abnormally high voltage from the third O2 sensor on bank 2. Indicates rich exhaust or wiring shorted to voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0166.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity / Slow Response (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P0166.plain: The ECU detects no switching or too slow a response from the third O2 sensor on bank 2. Typically aged or poisoned sensor or weak heater.

P0167.title: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 2 Sensor 3)
P0167.plain: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the heater circuit of the third O2 sensor on bank 2. Heater current out of range — open or shorted heater, blown fuse, wiring fault.

P0168.title: Fuel Temperature Too High
P0168.plain: Fuel temperature exceeds the safe maximum. Risk of fuel pump damage and injection imprecision.

P0169.title: Incorrect Fuel Composition
P0169.plain: Fuel composition (e.g. ethanol fraction on flex-fuel vehicles) outside expected range. Wrong fuel filled or sensor fault.
causes: Wrong fuel filled (e.g. E85 in non-flex)

P016A.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Air/Fuel Ratio Control
P016A.plain: ECU took longer than allowed to enter closed-loop air/fuel ratio control. Most often O2 sensor heater aging or coolant temperature reading wrong.

P016B.title: Closed Loop Air/Fuel Ratio Control At Limit - System Too Rich
P016B.plain: Closed-loop fuel trim hit its lean correction limit because mixture is structurally too rich. Likely fuel pressure too high, leaking injector, or O2 sensor reporting too lean.

P016C.title: Closed Loop Air/Fuel Ratio Control At Limit - System Too Lean
P016C.plain: Closed-loop fuel trim hit its rich correction limit because mixture is structurally too lean. Likely vacuum leak, low fuel pressure, or contaminated MAF.

P016D.title: Excessive Time To Enter Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control
P016D.plain: ECU took longer than allowed to close the loop on fuel pressure control. Pressure rise too slow at start.

P016E.title: Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control At Limit - Pressure Too High
P016E.plain: Closed-loop fuel pressure control hit its lower limit because rail pressure is structurally too high.

P016F.title: Closed Loop Fuel Pressure Control At Limit - Pressure Too Low
P016F.plain: Closed-loop fuel pressure control hit its upper limit because rail pressure is structurally too low.

P0170.title: Fuel Trim Malfunction (Bank 1)
P0170.plain: The ECU detects that short-term and long-term fuel trim values on bank 1 are outside acceptable limits. Engine cannot maintain stoichiometric mixture — typically a vacuum leak, fuel pressure issue, or failing MAF/O2 sensor.
causes: Fuel pressure too low or too high

P0171.title: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
P0171.plain: Long-term fuel trim on bank 1 is at the upper limit — the ECU is adding more fuel than baseline to maintain stoichiometric mixture but cannot reach target. Indicates unmetered air entering the intake or insufficient fuel delivery.
causes: Vacuum leak in intake or PCV system

P0172.title: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
P0172.plain: Long-term fuel trim on bank 1 is at the lower limit — the ECU is removing fuel from baseline but mixture remains too rich. Indicates excess fuel delivery, restricted air flow, or a faulty oxygen sensor reporting falsely lean.

P0173.title: Fuel Trim Malfunction Bank 2
P0173.plain: Fuel trims on bank 2 exceed adaptation limits in either lean or rich direction. The ECU cannot maintain stoichiometric mixture within calibrated boundaries.

P0174.title: System Too Lean (Bank 2)
P0174.plain: Same condition as P0171 but on bank 2 of a multi-bank engine (V6, V8, flat-six, etc.). When P0171 and P0174 appear together, the cause is usually a shared component such as the MAF sensor or a central vacuum leak rather than a bank-specific fault.
causes: Central vacuum leak (intake manifold gasket, brake booster)

P0175.title: System Too Rich (Bank 2)
P0175.plain: Same condition as P0172 but on bank 2. When paired with P0172, suspect shared causes (fuel pressure, blocked air filter); when alone, suspect a bank-specific injector or oxygen sensor.

P0176.title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0176.plain: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the flex-fuel composition sensor circuit. The sensor measures ethanol content (E0–E85) in the fuel; signal missing, shorted or out of plausible range.

P0177.title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Range / Performance
P0177.plain: The flex-fuel composition sensor signal is within electrical limits but does not match expected values for the current fuel mix or rate-of-change is implausible.

P0178.title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit Low Input
P0178.plain: The flex-fuel composition sensor signal is below the minimum threshold. Likely shorted to ground, open circuit or failed sensor.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0179.title: Fuel Composition Sensor Circuit High Input
P0179.plain: The flex-fuel composition sensor signal exceeds the maximum threshold. Likely shorted to voltage, open ground or failed sensor.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P017A.title: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P017A.plain: Generic electrical fault on cylinder head temperature sensor A (CHT sensor — used on engines without conventional ECT).

P017B.title: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Range/Performance
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P017C.title: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P017C.plain: CHT sensor A signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P017D.title: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P017D.plain: CHT sensor A signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P017E.title: Cylinder Head Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P017E.plain: Intermittent signal from CHT sensor A. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P017F.title: EVAP System Leak Detection Pump Module Air Filter Restricted
P017F.plain: Air filter on the EVAP leak detection pump module is restricted. Leak detection cannot establish reference pressure.

P0180.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Malfunction
P0180.plain: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the fuel temperature sensor A circuit. Fuel temperature input is missing or out of plausible range — typical for sensor failure or wiring open/short.

P0181.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range / Performance
P0181.plain: The fuel temperature sensor A signal is within electrical limits but inconsistent with plausibility checks (e.g. doesn't change with engine warmup, disagrees with ambient temperature).

P0182.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low Input
P0182.plain: The fuel temperature sensor A signal is below the minimum threshold. Likely shorted to ground or open circuit.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0183.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit High Input
P0183.plain: The fuel temperature sensor A signal exceeds the maximum threshold. Likely shorted to voltage, open ground or sensor open-circuit.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0184.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0184.plain: The ECU detects intermittent dropouts on the fuel temperature sensor A circuit. Loose connector, chafed wiring or sensor failing thermally.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0185.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Malfunction
P0185.plain: The ECU detects an electrical fault in the fuel temperature sensor B circuit (second sensor used on systems with separate supply/return temperature monitoring or twin-tank arrangements).

P0186.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Range / Performance
P0186.plain: Fuel temperature sensor B reading is within electrical limits but implausible (no warmup change, disagrees with sensor A or ambient).

P0187.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Low Input
P0187.plain: Fuel temperature sensor B signal below minimum. Shorted to ground or sensor open. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0188.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit High Input
P0188.plain: Fuel temperature sensor B signal exceeds maximum. Shorted to voltage, open ground or open sensor. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0189.title: Fuel Temperature Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P0189.plain: The ECU detects intermittent dropouts on the fuel temperature sensor B circuit. Loose connector, chafed wiring or sensor failing under thermal load.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P018A.title: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit
P018A.plain: Generic electrical fault on fuel pressure sensor B (second sensor, e.g. low-pressure side or alternative fuel system).

P018B.title: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit Range/Performance
P018B.plain: Fuel pressure sensor B reading implausible. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P018C.title: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit Low
P018C.plain: Fuel pressure sensor B signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P018D.title: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit High
P018D.plain: Fuel pressure sensor B signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P018E.title: Fuel Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P018E.plain: Intermittent signal from fuel pressure sensor B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P018F.title: Fuel System Over Pressure Relief Valve Frequent Activation
P018F.plain: The mechanical pressure relief valve has activated repeatedly within a short window — pressure regulation is failing more than once.

P0190.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit
P0190.plain: The ECU detects an out-of-range signal from the fuel rail pressure sensor. The voltage is outside calibrated min/max boundaries during normal operation.

P0191.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Range / Performance
P0191.plain: The fuel rail pressure sensor signal is within electrical limits but doesn't match commanded rail pressure under various engine loads. Common in common-rail diesel and GDI petrol engines.

P0192.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Low Input
P0192.plain: The ECU reads a voltage from the fuel rail pressure sensor below the calibrated minimum, indicating short to ground or open supply.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0193.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit High Input
P0193.plain: The ECU reads a voltage from the fuel rail pressure sensor above the calibrated maximum, indicating short to power or open ground reference.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0194.title: Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0194.plain: The ECU detects intermittent signal dropouts on the fuel rail pressure sensor. Loose connector, chafed wiring or sensor failing under vibration/heat.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0195.title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Malfunction
P0195.plain: The ECU detects a general electrical fault in the engine oil temperature sensor circuit. Signal missing, shorted or out of plausible range.

P0196.title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Range / Performance
P0196.plain: Engine oil temperature sensor signal is within electrical limits but implausible (no warmup change, contradicts coolant temperature).

P0197.title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Low
P0197.plain: Engine oil temperature sensor signal below minimum. Shorted to ground or open.

P0198.title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor High
P0198.plain: Engine oil temperature sensor signal exceeds maximum. Shorted to voltage, open ground or open sensor.

P0199.title: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Intermittent
P0199.plain: The ECU detects intermittent dropouts on the engine oil temperature sensor circuit. Loose connector, chafed wiring or sensor failing thermally.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P019A.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 1 Sensor 3
P019A.plain: Bank 1 sensor 3 O2 sensor reacts only after delay during rich-to-lean transitions. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P019B.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 1 Sensor 3
P019B.plain: Bank 1 sensor 3 O2 sensor reacts only after delay during lean-to-rich transitions. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P019C.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Rich to Lean Bank 2 Sensor 3
P019C.plain: Bank 2 sensor 3 O2 sensor reacts only after delay during rich-to-lean transitions. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P019D.title: O2 Sensor Delayed Response - Lean to Rich Bank 2 Sensor 3
P019D.plain: Bank 2 sensor 3 O2 sensor reacts only after delay during lean-to-rich transitions. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P019E.title: Alternative Fuel Tank A Pressure Sensor Circuit
P019E.plain: Generic electrical fault on alternative fuel tank A pressure sensor (CNG, LPG, hydrogen).

P019F.title: Alternative Fuel Tank A Pressure Sensor Performance
P019F.plain: Alternative fuel tank A pressure reading implausible.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P01A0.title: Alternative Fuel Tank A Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P01A0.plain: Alt fuel tank A pressure sensor signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P01A1.title: Alternative Fuel Tank A Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P01A1.plain: Alt fuel tank A pressure sensor signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P01A2.title: Alternative Fuel Tank A Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P01A2.plain: Intermittent signal from alt fuel tank A pressure sensor. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P01A3.title: Alternative Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit
P01A3.plain: Generic electrical fault on alternative fuel rail pressure sensor.

P01A4.title: Alternative Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Performance
P01A4.plain: Alt fuel rail pressure sensor reading implausible.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window
Sensor element contaminated by oil, soot or coolant

P01A5.title: Alternative Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P01A5.plain: Alt fuel rail pressure sensor signal voltage below expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P01A6.title: Alternative Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P01A6.plain: Alt fuel rail pressure sensor signal voltage above expected range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P01A7.title: Alternative Fuel Rail Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P01A7.plain: Intermittent signal from alt fuel rail pressure sensor. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P01A8.title: Alternative Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too Low
P01A8.plain: Alt fuel rail or system pressure below the expected operating range.

P01A9.title: Alternative Fuel Rail/System Pressure - Too High
P01A9.plain: Alt fuel rail or system pressure above the expected operating range.

P01AA.title: Alternative Fuel Tank Temperature Sensor Circuit
P01AA.plain: Generic electrical fault on alt fuel tank temperature sensor.

P01AB.title: Alternative Fuel Tank Temperature Sensor Range/Performance
P01AB.plain: Alt fuel tank temp sensor reading implausible.

P01F3.title: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage Bank 1 Sensor 4
P01F3.plain: Bank 1 sensor 4 O2 sensor signal voltage above expected range — short to power or sensor stuck high. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P01F4.title: O2 Sensor Circuit Slow Response Bank 1 Sensor 4
P01F4.plain: Bank 1 sensor 4 O2 sensor responds too slowly to mixture changes. Sensor aged. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P01F5.title: O2 Sensor Circuit No Activity Detected Bank 1 Sensor 4
P01F5.plain: Bank 1 sensor 4 O2 sensor shows no signal change despite operating conditions that should produce activity. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P01F6.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean Bank 1 Sensor 4
P01F6.plain: Bank 1 sensor 4 O2 sensor signal is biased low — sensor stuck reading lean regardless of true mixture. A drifted or sluggish lambda sensor lets the mixture run lean or rich without correction — fuel economy and emissions suffer immediately.

P01F7.title: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich Bank 1 Sensor 4

P0213.title: Cold Start Injector 1
P0213.plain: Fault detected on cold start injector 1 (auxiliary injector for cold engine starting on some older systems). A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.

P0214.title: Cold Start Injector 2
P0214.plain: Fault detected on cold start injector 2. A flow-deviating injector throws off cylinder balance — adjacent cylinders run leaner/richer to compensate, often masking the root cause until the trim limit is hit.

P0215.title: Engine Shutoff Solenoid
P0215.plain: Fault detected on the engine shutoff solenoid (used on diesels and some petrol engines to stop fuel flow at engine off).

P0216.title: Injector/Injection Timing Control Circuit
P0216.plain: Fault on the injection timing control circuit (used on mechanical injection pumps with electronic timing control).

P0217.title: Engine Coolant Over Temperature Condition
P0217.plain: Coolant temperature exceeded the safe maximum. Engine overheating event detected — risk of head gasket damage or seizure.

P0218.title: Transmission Fluid Over Temperature
P0218.plain: The TCM/PCM detected that automatic transmission fluid temperature exceeded the safe operating threshold. Continued operation accelerates wear on clutches and friction surfaces; many vehicles will engage a fail-safe mode and limit gear selection.

P0219.title: Engine Overspeed Condition
P0219.plain: The ECU recorded an engine speed above the manufacturer's redline limit. Typical causes are missed downshifts, mis-shifts on a manual gearbox, or runaway diesel events. The code is informational but may trigger fuel cut-off and protective derate.

P0220.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch "B" Circuit
P0220.plain: A general electrical fault was detected in the secondary (B) throttle or pedal position sensor circuit. Modern drive-by-wire systems use redundant TPS tracks; the ECU compares them and flags this code on the B channel when out of range.

P0221.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch "B" Range/Performance
P0221.plain: The B channel of the throttle or pedal position sensor reports values that do not correlate with the A channel or with engine load. Often caused by mechanical wear in the resistive track or by a sticking pedal/throttle plate.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0222.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch "B" Circuit Low Input
P0222.plain: The B channel voltage is below the lower diagnostic threshold, suggesting an open circuit, short to ground, or sensor element failure on track B.
causes: TPS B circuit open or shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0223.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch "B" Circuit High Input
P0223.plain: The B channel voltage is above the upper diagnostic threshold, typically caused by a short to supply voltage or a defective sensor.
causes: TPS B circuit shorted to supply voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0224.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Intermittent
P0224.plain: Intermittent signal from throttle position sensor B (electronic throttle systems use redundant sensors).
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0225.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit
P0225.plain: Generic electrical fault on throttle/pedal position sensor C (third sensor in some redundant designs).

P0226.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor C Circuit Range/Performance
P0226.plain: Throttle position sensor C signal is not tracking the other channels of the redundant TPS within tolerance. The ECU compares all three channels and detects rationality failure.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0227.title: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor/Switch C Circuit Low

P02CA.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Overboost Condition
P02CA.plain: Boost pressure on the secondary turbocharger/supercharger (B) on a sequential or twin-charged setup is above the upper threshold. Wastegate stuck closed, VGT vanes stuck, or boost pressure sensor reads high.

P02CB.title: Turbocharger/Supercharger B Underboost Condition
P02CB.plain: Boost pressure on the secondary turbocharger/supercharger (B) is below the lower threshold. Wastegate stuck open, charge-air leak, or VGT vanes stuck open.

P02CC.title: Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Min Limit
P02CC.plain: The PCM applies a per-cylinder injector offset (Mengenausgleich) to compensate for production-tolerance differences in injector flow rate. On cylinder 1 the learned correction has reached its minimum value — the injector is delivering significantly more fuel than the calibrated reference and the controller cannot trim it any further.
causes: Injector over-delivering — worn nozzle or stuck-open seat
Calibration code not programmed after replacement

P02CD.title: Cylinder 1 Fuel Injector A Offset Learning At Max Limit
P02CD.plain: The per-cylinder injector offset on cylinder 1 has reached its maximum value — the injector is delivering significantly less fuel than the calibrated reference, and the controller cannot trim it any further.
causes: Injector under-delivering — clogged nozzle or worn coil
Calibration code not programmed after replacement

P02E0.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit/Open
P02E0.plain: The drive circuit for the diesel intake air-flow control valve A is open. This valve (also called intake throttle, swirl flap actuator, or anti-shudder valve) closes the diesel intake to control airflow during regeneration and shutdown.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P02E1.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Performance
P02E1.plain: Diesel intake air-flow control A is electrically OK but does not move the throttle plate as commanded — typically carbon buildup or seized actuator.

P02E2.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit Low
P02E2.plain: Diesel intake air-flow control A drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P02E3.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Circuit High
P02E3.plain: Diesel intake air-flow control A drive line stuck high — short to B+. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P02E4.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Stuck Open
P02E4.plain: Diesel intake throttle A is mechanically stuck open — anti-shudder function on shutdown will not work and DPF regen airflow control is lost.
causes: Carbon buildup or broken return spring
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P02E5.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Stuck Closed
P02E5.plain: Diesel intake throttle A is mechanically stuck closed — engine starves of intake air.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P02E6.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit
P02E6.plain: A general electrical fault is reported on diesel intake throttle A position sensor — open, shorted, or out of plausibility.

P02E7.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P02E7.plain: Position sensor reads in range but plausibility check fails — does not match commanded throttle position.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P02E8.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit Low
P02E8.plain: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P02E9.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit High
P02E9.plain: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P02EA.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P02EA.plain: Position sensor signal jumps or drops out intermittently — connector or harness issue. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P02EB.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control Motor Current Range/Performance
P02EB.plain: Motor current draw of the diesel intake throttle A actuator does not match the calibrated map for the commanded position — high friction, partial short, or stiction from carbon.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P02EC.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control System - High Air Flow Detected
P02EC.plain: Air flow through diesel intake throttle A is higher than the commanded set point — flap leaking past the seat or stuck partly open.

P02ED.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow A Control System - Low Air Flow Detected
P02ED.plain: Air flow through diesel intake throttle A is lower than the commanded set point — flap stuck partly closed.

P02EE.title: Cylinder 1 Injector Circuit Range/Performance
P02EE.plain: The cylinder 1 injector drive circuit is electrically OK but the response (current ramp, dwell time, or peak voltage) does not match the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or wiring corrosion.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P02EF.title: Cylinder 2 Injector Circuit Range/Performance
P02EF.plain: The cylinder 2 injector drive circuit is electrically OK but the response (current ramp, dwell time, or peak voltage) does not match the calibrated profile — typically a high-resistance solenoid winding or wiring corrosion.

P02FA.title: Diesel Intake Air Flow Position Sensor Minimum/Maximum Stop Performance
P02FA.plain: The diesel intake throttle position sensor does not reach the calibrated minimum or maximum stop value during a self-test sweep — typically sensor wear, mechanical stop misalignment, or a sticky throttle plate.

P02FB.title: Cold Start Fuel Injection Control Circuit/Open
P02FB.plain: The drive circuit for the cold-start auxiliary fuel injector or the cold-start ECU output is open. Some diesels use an extra cold-start injector to inject fuel into the intake manifold during very cold starts.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P02FC.plain: Cold-start injector drive line stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
