causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P05DB.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Open
P05DB.plain: The brake pedal position sensor B has an open control circuit. The ECU loses analogue feedback about pedal travel - used by stop-start, regenerative braking and adaptive cruise to coordinate engine, motor and friction brakes.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P05DC.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Range or Performance
P05DC.plain: Same as P057B on sensor B.

P05DD.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Low
P05DD.plain: Same as P057C on sensor B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P05DE.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit High
P05DE.plain: Same as P057D on sensor B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P05DF.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor B Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P05DF.plain: Same as P057E on sensor B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P05E0.title: Brake Pedal Position Sensor A and B Correlation
P05E0.plain: Brake-by-wire and electronic brake systems use two redundant pedal position sensors. Their readings disagree by more than the diagnostic tolerance - one or both has drifted, or wiring picks up noise on one channel.
causes: One sensor has drifted out of tolerance

P05E1.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor A Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P05E1.plain: The high-side refrigerant pressure sensor A reports intermittent or erratic signal - typically a connector or harness fault on the sensor that lives close to the compressor.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P05E2.title: A/C Refrigerant Pressure Sensor B Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P05E2.plain: The high-side refrigerant pressure sensor B reports intermittent or erratic signal - typically a connector or harness fault on the sensor that lives close to the compressor.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P05E3.title: Park Brake Sensor or Switch Circuit
P05E3.plain: The park brake apply switch or position sensor reports a circuit fault. The ECU loses the indication whether the parking brake is engaged - relevant for stop-start, hill-hold, and certain shift-interlock strategies.

P05E4.title: Park Brake Sensor or Switch Circuit Low
P05E4.plain: Same as P05E3 with the signal shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P05E5.title: Park Brake Sensor or Switch Circuit High
P05E5.plain: Same as P05E3 with the signal shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P05E6.title: Park Brake Sensor or Switch Circuit Range or Performance
P05E6.plain: Same as P05E3 with input in plausible range yet not matching expected behaviour.

P05E7.title: Park Brake Sensor or Switch Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P05E7.plain: Same as P05E3 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P05E8.title: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit Open
P05E8.plain: The oil bypass valve - which routes oil around the cooler to speed up warm-up - has an open control circuit. Without it, oil temperature rise during cold-start is slower than calibrated.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P05E9.title: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit Low
P05E9.plain: Same as P05E8 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P05EA.title: Engine Oil Bypass Valve Control Circuit High
P05EA.plain: Same as P05E8 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P05EB.title: Cold Start SCR NOx Catalyst Inlet Temperature Too Low
P05EB.plain: Same as P22FF but specifically during the cold-start window - the SCR catalyst inlet temperature does not reach the threshold needed for NOx reduction in the cold-start phase, so reductant injection cannot be enabled.
causes: Heat-up strategy not bringing exhaust to temp

P05EC.title: Cold Start Injection Timing Performance
P05EC.plain: During cold-start the ECU adjusts injection timing (post-injection on diesels, intake-stroke timing on direct-injection petrols) to support catalyst light-off. The strategy does not deliver the expected timing - injector response slow or sensor offset.

P05ED.title: Reductant Heater Control Module Supply Voltage
P05ED.plain: The reductant (AdBlue) heater control module - which warms tank, lines and injector to keep AdBlue from freezing - reports its supply voltage outside the calibrated window.

P05EE.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Open
P05EE.plain: The supply line that powers the AdBlue dosing pump is open. Without supply the pump cannot deliver reductant pressure - dosing is suspended and NOx emissions can drift out of compliance.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P05EF.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Low
P05EF.plain: Same as P05EE with the supply voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P05F0.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit High
P05F0.plain: Same as P05EE with the supply voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P05F1.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Stuck On
P05F1.plain: The supply relay or driver for the reductant pump is welded or stuck active - the pump runs continuously, even with the engine off, draining the battery and over-pressurising the dosing circuit.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P05F2.title: Reductant Pump Supply Voltage Circuit Stuck Off
P05F2.plain: Same as P05EE with the supply stuck off - relay does not energise on command.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P05F3.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Open
P05F3.plain: The power relay that supplies the entire exhaust aftertreatment system (DOC, DPF, SCR sensors and heaters) reports an open control circuit. Aftertreatment effectively goes offline.
causes: Open in relay control or harness
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P05F4.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Low
P05F4.plain: Same as P05F3 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P05F5.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit High
P05F5.plain: Same as P05F3 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P05F6.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Stuck On
P05F6.plain: The aftertreatment power relay is stuck on - aftertreatment electronics stay powered after key-off, draining the battery.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P05F7.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Power Relay Control Circuit Stuck Off
P05F7.plain: Same as P05F3 with the relay not engaging on command.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P05F8.title: Reductant Heater Control Module Performance
P05F8.plain: The reductant heater module is electrically intact but does not deliver the expected thermal effect - heater elements aged, supply line resistance, or thermostat sensor offset.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P05F9.title: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit
P05F9.plain: A general circuit fault on the stop-start status signal - the bus or hardwire that tells other modules whether the engine is auto-stopped or running.

P05FA.title: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit Low
P05FA.plain: Same as P05F9 with the signal shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P05FB.title: Stop-Start Status Signal Circuit High
P05FB.plain: Same as P05F9 with the signal shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P05FC.title: Cold Start Fuel Pressure Performance Bank 2
P05FC.plain: During cold-start the ECU runs an elevated rail pressure on direct-injection systems for better cold spray atomisation. The pressure target on bank 2 is not reached within the calibrated time window - typical for a high-pressure pump that loses output when cold or a pressure regulator with cold-stickiness.
causes: HP pump output low when cold

P05FD.title: Turbocharger Boost Control A Temperature Too High
P05FD.plain: The boost control actuator A reports excessive operating temperature - typically heat soak from the turbo housing, prolonged high-load operation, or insufficient cooling. Boost is derated to protect the actuator electronics.

P05FE.title: Active Grille Air Shutter C Performance Stuck Off
P05FE.plain: Active Grille Air Shutter C Performance Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position. Active grille shutters manage airflow for engine cooling and aerodynamics.
causes: Shutter jammed by debris or ice
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P05FF.title: Brake Pressure Sensor and Brake Pedal Position Sensor Correlation
P05FF.plain: The brake pressure sensor and pedal position sensor disagree by more than the diagnostic tolerance - one indicates pedal action without the other showing pressure, or vice versa.

P0600.title: Serial Communication Link
P0600.plain: A general fault on a serial communication link - typically used by older single-wire diagnostic protocols (KWP2000, ISO 9141) before CAN became universal. ECU has lost or corrupted communication with another module.
causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P0601.title: Internal Control Module Memory Check Sum Error
P0601.plain: The ECU's internal memory checksum does not match the expected value at startup — the firmware/calibration in flash has become corrupt. Often appears after a failed flash, low battery during programming, or genuine module hardware failure.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P0602.title: Control Module Programming Error
P0602.plain: The ECU is reporting that it is missing required calibration data — typically appears after a virgin module is installed but never coded/programmed for the vehicle, or after a flash that did not write all blocks.
causes: Replacement ECU not coded to vehicle

P0603.title: Internal Control Module Keep Alive Memory (KAM) Error
P0603.plain: The ECU detected a fault in its KAM (battery-backed memory used to store adaptations and DTCs). Often appears after battery disconnect or low battery; persistent codes indicate an internal ECU fault.
causes: Battery disconnected or voltage too low
Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P0604.title: Internal Control Module Random Access Memory (RAM) Error
P0604.plain: ECU self-test detected a RAM fault during runtime checks. This is an internal ECU defect; replacement or reflash with manufacturer support is generally required.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P0605.title: Internal Control Module Read Only Memory (ROM) Error
P0605.plain: ECU self-test detected a ROM/checksum failure on the program memory. The control software cannot be trusted; vehicle typically defaults to limp-home with reduced function.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P0606.title: ECM/PCM Processor Fault
P0606.plain: The ECU's internal processor self-test has failed. This is a hard module fault — the ECU usually triggers limp-home mode and may not respond to scan tools fully until replaced or repaired.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P0607.title: Control Module Performance
P0607.plain: The ECM performs an internal self-test and detects a processor or memory performance fault that does not fit the more specific P0601 to P0606 codes.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P0608.title: Control Module VSS Output A
P0608.plain: The vehicle speed signal output from the control module to other systems is faulty. Other modules expect a speed signal that the ECM no longer provides correctly.

P0609.title: Control Module VSS Output B
P0609.plain: A fault is detected on the secondary vehicle speed signal output (VSS B) that the ECU sends to other modules (instrument cluster, ABS, transmission). Output level inconsistent with the internal speed value.

P060A.title: Internal Control Module Monitoring Processor Performance
P060A.plain: Modern ECUs have a separate watchdog or monitoring processor that supervises the main processor. This processor reports a self-diagnosis fault - typically a watchdog event, ROM/RAM mismatch, or check-sum error in its monitor section. The ECU runs in a safety-fallback mode until repair.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P060B.title: Internal Control Module A and D Processing Performance
P060B.plain: The ECU's analog-to-digital converter does not deliver consistent results - typically reference voltage drift, multiplexer fault, or noise on the analog ground.

P060C.title: Internal Control Module Main Processor Performance
P060C.plain: The ECU main processor self-diagnosis flagged a performance fault - watchdog, ROM check, or instruction-set self-test failed. Engine runs on safety strategy.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P060D.title: Internal Control Module Accelerator Pedal Position Performance
P060D.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "accelerator pedal position" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

P060E.title: Internal Control Module Throttle Position Performance
P060E.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "throttle position" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

P060F.title: Internal Control Module Coolant Temperature Performance
P060F.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "engine coolant temperature" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

P0610.title: Control Module Vehicle Options Error
P0610.plain: The ECU's stored vehicle option configuration is invalid or does not match the connected hardware. Common after replacing or swapping a control module without proper coding/configuration.

P0611.title: Fuel Injector Control Module Performance
P0611.plain: Modern direct-injection systems use a dedicated injector driver module that generates the high-voltage charge pulses needed to open piezo or solenoid injectors. The module reports an internal performance fault.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P0612.title: Fuel Injector Control Module Relay Control
P0612.plain: A circuit fault on the relay that powers the injector driver module - either control line or contact integrity issue.

P0613.title: TCM Processor
P0613.plain: The transmission control module performs an internal self-test and detects a processor performance fault.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P0614.title: ECM and TCM Incompatible
P0614.plain: The ECM and TCM exchange identification or calibration data over the powertrain bus and detect that they are not a valid pair - typically appears after replacing one of the modules with a unit from a different vehicle variant.

P0615.title: Starter Relay Circuit
P0615.plain: General electrical fault on the starter relay control circuit driven by the ECU/PCM. Typical symptom is a no-crank or intermittent crank condition.

P0616.title: Starter Relay A Circuit Low
P0616.plain: The control line for starter relay A is shorted to ground - the ECU drives the relay and measures voltage too low.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0617.title: Starter Relay Circuit High
P0617.plain: The starter relay control circuit voltage is above the upper threshold — short to supply or stuck driver.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0618.title: Alternative Fuel Control Module KAM Error
P0618.plain: The control module for alternative fuel (CNG, LPG, hydrogen) reports a Keep-Alive-Memory error - persistent calibration values are corrupt or unreadable. Adaptive learning is reset.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P0619.title: Alternative Fuel Control Module RAM and ROM Error
P0619.plain: The alternative fuel control module reports an internal RAM or ROM check failure - module no longer trustworthy.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P061A.title: Internal Control Module Torque Performance
P061A.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "engine torque" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

P061B.title: Internal Control Module Torque Calculation Performance
P061B.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "torque calculation" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

P061C.title: Internal Control Module Engine RPM Performance
P061C.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "engine speed (RPM)" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

P061D.title: Internal Control Module Engine Air Mass Performance
P061D.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "intake air mass" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

P061E.title: Internal Control Module Brake Signal Performance
P061E.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "brake signal" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

P061F.title: Internal Control Module Throttle Actuator Controller Performance
P061F.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "throttle actuator control" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

P0620.title: Generator Control Circuit
P0620.plain: General electrical fault detected in the alternator/generator control circuit. The ECU regulates field excitation on most modern alternators; a fault here causes charging issues and may set additional battery voltage codes.

P0621.title: Generator Lamp L Control Circuit
P0621.plain: The control circuit for the generator warning lamp output (L terminal) reports a fault.

P0622.title: Generator Field F Control Circuit
P0622.plain: The control circuit for the generator field terminal (F) reports a fault. The ECM cannot regulate field current as expected.

P0623.title: Generator Lamp Control Circuit
P0623.plain: Generic generator warning lamp control circuit fault, often used where the lamp terminal designation is not L or where multiple lamps share a single output.

P0624.title: Fuel Cap Lamp Control Circuit
P0624.plain: The control circuit for the fuel cap warning lamp reports a fault. The ECM cannot drive the indicator that warns of an open or loose fuel cap.

P0625.title: Generator Field Terminal Circuit Low
P0625.plain: Voltage on the alternator F terminal (field excitation) is below threshold — open or short to ground in the excitation path.
causes: Field circuit open or shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0626.title: Generator Field/F Terminal Circuit Performance
P0626.plain: The generator field circuit response does not match command. Field current ramps slowly, drifts or fails to reach commanded values during regulation.

P0627.title: Fuel Pump "A" Control Circuit Open
P0627.plain: The ECU detected an open circuit in the fuel pump A control output. With no pump operation the engine cannot run; this code is often paired with no-start and no fuel pressure.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P0628.title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Low
P0628.plain: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Low: the control-circuit voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0629.title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit High
P0629.plain: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit High: the control-circuit voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P062A.title: Fuel Pump A Control Circuit Range or Performance
P062A.plain: The control output to the primary fuel pump A is electrically intact yet response and fuel pressure response do not match - typically a worn pump, a clogged strainer, or a partially shorted PWM driver.

P062B.title: Internal Control Module Fuel Injector Control Performance
P062B.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "fuel injector control" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

P062C.title: Internal Control Module Vehicle Speed Performance
P062C.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "vehicle speed" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.

P062D.title: Fuel Injector Driver Circuit Performance Bank 1
P062D.plain: The injector driver stage on bank 1 - the high-side or low-side switching transistor that fires the injectors - reports a performance fault. Typical for a partial driver short, drift in the boost capacitor, or supply ripple under load.

P062E.title: Fuel Injector Driver Circuit Performance Bank 2
P062E.plain: The injector driver stage on bank 2 - the high-side or low-side switching transistor that fires the injectors - reports a performance fault. Typical for a partial driver short, drift in the boost capacitor, or supply ripple under load.

P062F.title: Internal Control Module EEPROM Error
P062F.plain: The ECU's EEPROM (persistent calibration storage) reports a check-sum or write error. Calibration values may be corrupted - the ECU runs on safe defaults until repair.

P0630.title: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible ECM or PCM
P0630.plain: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible ECM or PCM: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P0631.title: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible TCM
P0631.plain: VIN Not Programmed or Incompatible TCM: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P0632.title: Odometer Not Programmed ECM or PCM
P0632.plain: The odometer value stored in the ECM/PCM is missing or implausible - typical after a module replacement without odometer programming, or after persistent storage corruption.

P0633.title: Immobiliser Key Not Programmed
P0633.plain: The immobiliser system rejects the current key because it is not programmed to this vehicle. Engine start is inhibited.

P0634.title: Control Module Internal Temperature A Too High
P0634.plain: Control Module Internal Temperature A Too High: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P0635.title: Power Steering Control Circuit
P0635.plain: A general circuit fault is detected on the power steering control output - typically the line that the ECU uses to request raised idle when steering load is high, or to enable an electric pump.

P0636.title: Power Steering Control Circuit Low
P0636.plain: Same as P0635 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0637.title: Power Steering Control Circuit High
P0637.plain: Same as P0635 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0638.title: Throttle Actuator Control Range or Performance Bank 1
P0638.plain: The drive-by-wire throttle actuator on bank 1 does not respond as commanded - actuator slow, gearing slipping, or position feedback offset against actual blade angle.

P0639.title: Throttle Actuator Control Range or Performance Bank 2
P0639.plain: The drive-by-wire throttle actuator on bank 2 does not respond as commanded - actuator slow, gearing slipping, or position feedback offset against actual blade angle.

P063A.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A
P063A.plain: A general circuit fault is detected on the alternator voltage sense line A - the line over which the regulator measures battery-side voltage to set charging output.
causes: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold

P063B.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A Range or Performance
P063B.plain: Same as P063A with the sense voltage in plausible range yet not matching the alternator output - high contact resistance or wrong calibration.
causes: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold

P063C.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A Low
P063C.plain: Same as P063A with the sense voltage below the plausible range.
causes: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold

P063D.title: Generator Voltage Sense Circuit A High
P063D.plain: Same as P063A with the sense voltage above the plausible range.
causes: Pack cell imbalance approaching service threshold

P063E.title: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 1
P063E.plain: Auto Configuration Throttle Input Not Present Bank 1: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P063F.title: Auto Configuration Engine Coolant Temperature Input Not Present
P063F.plain: Auto Configuration Engine Coolant Temperature Input Not Present: the control module has detected this fault condition.

P0640.title: Intake Air Heater Control Circuit
P0640.plain: A general circuit fault on the intake air heater control - the ECU cannot drive the grid heater at cold-start.

P0641.title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit Open
P0641.plain: The 5 V reference voltage that the ECU supplies to multiple sensors (TPS, MAP, accelerator pedal, etc.) has dropped out or is open-circuit. Symptoms cascade — many sensor codes appear at once, all related to the same reference rail.
causes: Reference wire shorted to ground (one defective sensor pulls the rail down)
Pin pushed back out of connector body

P0642.title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit Low
P0642.plain: The 5 V reference voltage on the A circuit (used by multiple sensors) is below threshold — short to ground or excessive current draw by a single sensor pulling the rail down.
causes: Sensor or harness shorted to ground
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0643.title: Sensor Reference Voltage "A" Circuit High
P0643.plain: 5 V reference rail A above threshold — short to a higher voltage source. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Sensor or harness shorted to higher voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0644.title: Driver Display Serial Communication Circuit
P0644.plain: The serial communication line to the driver display (instrument cluster, MIL/check-engine warning) shows a circuit fault. Driver may not see warning lights as expected.
causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P0645.title: A and C Clutch Relay Control Circuit
P0645.plain: A general circuit fault on the A/C clutch relay control - the line over which the ECU engages the magnetic clutch to drive the A/C compressor.

P0646.title: A and C Clutch Relay Control Circuit Low
P0646.plain: Same as P0645 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0647.title: A and C Clutch Relay Control Circuit High
P0647.plain: Same as P0645 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0648.title: Immobilizer Lamp Control Circuit
P0648.plain: Immobilizer Lamp Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.

P0649.title: Speed Control Lamp Control Circuit
P0649.plain: Speed Control Lamp Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.

P064A.title: Fuel Pump Control Module A
P064A.plain: A general fault is detected on the dedicated fuel pump control module A. Used on PWM-controlled returnless fuel systems to vary pump speed against demand. The module reports an internal performance issue.

P064B.title: PTO Control Module
P064B.plain: A general fault on the power take-off (PTO) control module - reports internal performance issue or communication trouble. Affects vehicles with auxiliary mechanical drives (cranes, snow ploughs, hydraulic pumps).

P064C.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1
P064C.plain: A general fault is detected on the first glow plug control module - typically a self-diagnosis flag for an internal driver, supply, or watchdog issue.

P064D.title: Internal Control Module O2 Sensor Processor Performance Bank 1
P064D.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "oxygen sensor processing, bank 1" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P064E.title: Internal Control Module O2 Sensor Processor Performance Bank 2
P064E.plain: An internal self-test in the control module reports a fault in its processing of the "oxygen sensor processing, bank 2" value. The module computes and cross-checks this value redundantly inside its own processor; when the results disagree, the code sets. It points to a hardware or software fault inside the module itself, not to a defect of the external sensor. Causes are an internal processor or memory fault, corrupted control-module software, or low or disturbed module supply voltage.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P064F.title: Unauthorized Software or Calibration Detected
P064F.plain: The ECU's secure boot or signature check has detected calibration data that is not signed by the manufacturer - typically appears after chip-tuning or unauthorised flash programming. The ECU may run on safe defaults or refuse to start.

P0650.title: Malfunction Indicator Lamp Control Circuit Malfunction
P0650.plain: A fault in the wiring or control circuit between the ECU and the malfunction indicator lamp (MIL). The MIL may stay on permanently, fail to light at key-on, or flicker — the OBD-II self-check on the bulb itself failed.
causes: Wiring fault between ECU and cluster

P0651.title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit Open
P0651.plain: The 5-volt sensor reference rail B is open — the module supplies no voltage on this circuit. Every sensor powered from reference B loses its supply and reads invalid, so the ECU substitutes default values and may limit engine operation. Causes: a broken reference wire, a disconnected connector, or an internal open in the module's voltage regulator for rail B.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0652.title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit Low
P0652.plain: Same as P0651 with the reference rail shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0653.title: Sensor Reference Voltage B Circuit High
P0653.plain: Same as P0651 with the reference rail shorted to supply or above the design voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0654.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit Open
P0654.plain: The engine RPM signal output that the ECU sends to other modules (tachometer, transmission, ABS) has an open circuit.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0655.title: Engine Hot Lamp Output Control Circuit
P0655.plain: A circuit fault on the engine-hot warning lamp output - the high-coolant-temperature warning may not light when needed.

P0656.title: Fuel Level Output Circuit
P0656.plain: A circuit fault on the fuel level output that the ECU sends to other modules (instrument cluster, range estimator).

P0657.title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit Open
P0657.plain: The supply rail that powers a group of actuators (typically injectors, EGR, throttle motor) is open. Multiple downstream actuators stop working.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0658.title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit Low
P0658.plain: Same as P0657 with the supply voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0659.title: Actuator Supply Voltage A Circuit High
P0659.plain: Same as P0657 with the supply voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P065A.title: Generator System Performance
P065A.plain: A general performance fault in the alternator system - charging output too low or too high under normal load conditions, often caused by a worn brush, a failing regulator, or harness resistance.

P065B.title: Generator A Control Circuit Range or Performance
P065B.plain: The PWM control line to the alternator A regulator does not deliver the expected charging response - high contact resistance, regulator drift, or wrong calibration.

P065C.title: Generator A Mechanical Performance
P065C.plain: The alternator A reports a mechanical performance issue - typically a slipping belt, worn pulley clutch, or seizing rotor that causes the output to lag behind speed.

P065D.title: Reductant System Malfunction Lamp Control Circuit
P065D.plain: A circuit fault on the AdBlue malfunction warning lamp output - regulatory in many regions to alert the driver of NOx aftertreatment problems.

P065E.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Performance Bank 1
P065E.plain: The intake manifold tuning valve (IMT) on bank 1 - which switches the intake runners between long and short paths for torque optimisation - is electrically intact yet does not move as commanded. Carbon build-up, broken linkage, or seized actuator.
causes: IMT valve stuck due to carbon

P065F.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Performance Bank 2
P065F.plain: The intake manifold tuning valve (IMT) on bank 2 - which switches the intake runners between long and short paths for torque optimisation - is electrically intact yet does not move as commanded. Carbon build-up, broken linkage, or seized actuator.
causes: IMT valve stuck due to carbon

P0660.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Open Bank 1
P0660.plain: The control line of the IMT valve on bank 1 is open - the ECU cannot drive the valve. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0661.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Low Bank 1
P0661.plain: Same as P0660 with the control line shorted to ground. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0662.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit High Bank 1
P0662.plain: Same as P0660 with the control line shorted to supply. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0663.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Open Bank 2
P0663.plain: The control line of the IMT valve on bank 2 is open - the ECU cannot drive the valve. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0664.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit Low Bank 2
P0664.plain: Same as P0661 on bank 2. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0665.title: Intake Manifold Tuning Valve Control Circuit High Bank 2
P0665.plain: Same as P0662 on bank 2. The intake manifold runner control (IMRC) flaps tune intake geometry for filling efficiency across the rpm range; stuck flaps cost part-load torque and can set lean codes.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0666.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0666.plain: A general circuit fault on the ECU's internal temperature sensor A - the sensor that monitors module operating temperature for thermal protection.

P0667.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Range or Performance
P0667.plain: Same as P0666 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine bay environment.

P0668.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P0668.plain: Same as P0666 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0669.title: Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P0669.plain: Same as P0666 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P066A.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Control Circuit Low
P066A.plain: The control line for the glow plug on cylinder 1 is shorted to ground or the plug is internally shorted.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P066B.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Control Circuit High
P066B.plain: The control line for the glow plug on cylinder 1 is open or shorted to supply - the plug cannot be heated.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P066C.plain: The control line for the glow plug on cylinder 2 is shorted to ground or the plug is internally shorted.

P066D.title: Cylinder 2 Glow Plug Control Circuit High
P066D.plain: The control line for the glow plug on cylinder 2 is open or shorted to supply - the plug cannot be heated.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P066E.title: Cylinder 3 Glow Plug Control Circuit Low
P066E.plain: The control line for the glow plug on cylinder 3 is shorted to ground or the plug is internally shorted.

P066F.title: Cylinder 3 Glow Plug Control Circuit High
P066F.plain: The control line for the glow plug on cylinder 3 is open or shorted to supply - the plug cannot be heated.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0670.title: Glow Plug Module Control Circuit
P0670.plain: The control circuit between the engine controller and the glow plug control module reports a fault. The ECU can no longer reliably command the module that drives the glow plugs, so cold-start pre-heating may not run. On a diesel this causes hard starting, white smoke, and rough running until warm. Causes: open or shorted wiring between ECU and glow plug module, a failed module, or a power/ground fault at the module.

P0671.title: Cylinder 1 Glow Plug Circuit
P0671.plain: An electrical fault is present in the glow plug circuit for cylinder 1. The glow plug control module cannot drive this plug correctly — open circuit, short, or out-of-range resistance — so cylinder 1 is not pre-heated. On a cold start this causes hard starting, white smoke, and a misfire-like rough run until the engine warms. Causes: a failed glow plug, a broken supply lead to that plug, corrosion at the plug connector, or a faulty module output for cylinder 1.

P0683.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 to PCM Communication Circuit
P0683.plain: Glow Plug Control Module 1 to PCM Communication Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects diesel cold-start preheating.
causes: Open or short on communication wire
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P0684.title: Glow Plug Control Module 1 to PCM Communication Range or Performance
P0684.plain: Same as P0683 with the communication signals in plausible range yet not matching expected protocol or content.
causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

P0685.title: ECM or PCM Power Relay Control Circuit Open
P0685.plain: The control circuit of the main ECM/PCM power relay is open - the ECU can lose power on shutdown sequence or fail to wake up at next start.
causes: Open in relay control or harness
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0686.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Control Circuit Open
P0686.plain: The control circuit for the ECM main power relay is open. Without this relay, the controller cannot maintain its keep-alive supply.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P0687.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Open
P0687.plain: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Open: the circuit is open. Likely a broken wire, disconnected connector, or failed component.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body

P0688.title: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit High
P0688.plain: ECM/PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0689.title: ECM or PCM Power Relay Sense Circuit Low
P0689.plain: The voltage sense line that confirms the main ECU power relay has actually closed reads low - either the relay is not closing or the sense line is shorted to ground.

P06EC.plain: The fuel injector control module has reported a fault to the ECM and requested MIL illumination. Read the FICM-side code for the actual fault.

P06ED.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit Low
P06ED.plain: Same as P0654 with the output line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P06EE.title: Engine RPM Output Circuit High
P06EE.plain: Same as P0654 with the output line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P06EF.title: Engine Restart Performance
P06EF.plain: After a stop-start auto-stop the engine takes longer than calibrated to restart, or restart is missed. Possible causes are weak starter, low battery state of charge, weak crank position signal at low RPM, or a fuel rail that lost prime.

P06F0.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit
P06F0.plain: A general circuit fault on the internal temperature sensor of the reductant control module.

P06F1.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Range or Performance
P06F1.plain: Same as P06F0 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine bay environment.

P06F2.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P06F2.plain: Same as P06F0 with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P06F3.title: Reductant Control Module Internal Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P06F3.plain: Same as P06F0 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P06F4.title: Stop-Start Mode Lamp Control Circuit
P06F4.plain: Stop-Start Mode Lamp Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.

P06F5.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2
P06F5.plain: A general fault on the second glow plug control module - used on engines with two banks of glow plugs.

P06F6.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Control Circuit Open
P06F6.plain: The control circuit driving glow plug control module 2 is open. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P06F7.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Control Circuit Low
P06F7.plain: Same as P06F6 with the control line shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P06F8.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Control Circuit High
P06F8.plain: Same as P06F6 with the control line shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P06F9.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 System Voltage
P06F9.plain: Glow Plug Control Module 2 System Voltage: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects diesel cold-start preheating.

P06FA.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Performance
P06FA.plain: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. This affects diesel cold-start preheating.

P06FB.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Memory Checksum Error
P06FB.plain: Glow Plug Control Module 2 Memory Checksum Error: the control module has detected this fault condition. This affects diesel cold-start preheating.
causes: Module software outdated, reflash may resolve

P06FC.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 to PCM Communication Circuit
P06FC.plain: Glow Plug Control Module 2 to PCM Communication Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit. This affects diesel cold-start preheating.
causes: Open or short on communication wire
Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P06FD.title: Glow Plug Control Module 2 to PCM Communication Range or Performance
causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P06FE.title: Cold Start Diesel Intake Air Flow Control Performance
P06FE.plain: During cold-start of a diesel engine the ECU controls intake airflow (e.g. anti-shudder valve, swirl flaps) to support smooth ignition. The control loop does not deliver the expected airflow - flap stuck or position offset.

P06FF.title: Economy Mode Lamp Control Circuit
P06FF.plain: Economy Mode Lamp Control Circuit: the control circuit has an electrical fault.

P0700.title: Transmission Control System Malfunction
P0700.plain: A request from the transmission control module (TCM) to illuminate the MIL. P0700 itself carries no specific information — it is a wrapper that tells the engine ECU "the TCM has a code". Read the TCM directly to find the actual transmission DTC.
causes: TCM has a sub-code that needs to be read separately

P0701.title: Transmission Control System Range/Performance
P0701.plain: The TCM has detected a transmission performance issue without identifying a specific component fault — typically slip outside expected range, shift timing outside spec, or a hydraulic issue not yet diagnosed by a more specific code.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0702.title: Transmission Control System Electrical
P0702.plain: A general electrical fault is detected in the transmission control system. The TCM has flagged a circuit problem (open, short, or supply issue) without specifying which component. Look up additional codes from the TCM for detail.

P0703.title: Brake Switch B Circuit
P0703.plain: A general circuit fault on the secondary brake switch B - typically used as redundant input for safety-critical functions like cruise control cancellation and shift-interlock.

P0704.title: Clutch Switch Input Circuit
P0704.plain: A circuit fault on the clutch pedal position switch input - used by the ECU to inhibit cruise control, allow cranking, and time gear-shift events on manual transmissions.

P0705.title: Transmission Range Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0705.plain: The transmission range sensor (PRNDL switch / inhibitor switch) signal is implausible — multiple positions active simultaneously, or no position recognized. Engine may refuse to start unless P or N is detected.

P0706.title: Transmission Range Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0706.plain: The transmission range sensor reports a position that is implausible against vehicle speed and engine state. Often caused by sensor misadjustment or worn contacts.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0707.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Low
P0707.plain: The primary transmission range sensor A (PRNDL switch position) reports voltage below the plausible range - signal shorted to ground or sensor fault.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0708.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit High
P0708.plain: Same as P0707 with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0709.title: Transmission Range Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0709.plain: Same as P0707 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P070A.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit
P070A.plain: A general circuit fault on the transmission fluid level sensor.

P070B.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit Range or Performance
P070B.plain: Same as P070A with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.

P070C.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit Low
P070C.plain: Same as P070A with the signal voltage below the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P070D.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit High
P070D.plain: Same as P070A with the signal voltage above the plausible range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P070E.title: Transmission Fluid Level Sensor Circuit Intermittent or Erratic
P070E.plain: Same as P070A with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P070F.title: Transmission Fluid Level Too Low
P070F.plain: The fluid level sensor reports level below the safe minimum - risk of pump cavitation, hydraulic pressure loss and gearbox damage. Drive carefully or stop and refill.

P0710.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P0710.plain: The transmission fluid temperature sensor A signal is missing or out of range. Used by shift logic to adapt timings to fluid viscosity.

P0711.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range or Performance
P0711.plain: The transmission fluid temperature sensor A reports a value within plausible range yet not matching the engine model - sensor drift or slow response.

P0712.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor Circuit Low
P0712.plain: ATF temperature sensor signal voltage below the lower threshold — open, short to ground, or sensor fault.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0713.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor Circuit High
P0713.plain: ATF temperature sensor signal voltage above the upper threshold — short to supply or sensor fault. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0714.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0714.plain: Same as P0711 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0715.title: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor "A" Circuit Malfunction
P0715.plain: The transmission input speed (turbine) sensor signal is missing or implausible. Without this signal, the TCM cannot detect torque converter slip or calculate gear ratio in real time, and shifts become harsh.

P0716.title: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor "A" Circuit Range/Performance
P0716.plain: The transmission input/turbine speed sensor signal is implausible compared to engine RPM and current gear ratio. Often caused by a failing sensor, debris on the reluctor, or wiring noise.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0717.title: Input/Turbine Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
P0717.plain: TCM detects no signal from the input/turbine speed sensor while the engine is running and the transmission is in gear. Without this signal the TCM cannot compute slip, and the transmission usually enters limp mode.

P0718.title: Input or Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0718.plain: Input or Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent: the signal is intermittent or erratic. Often a loose connector or chafed wiring; a wiggle test often locates it.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0719.title: Brake Switch B Circuit Low
P0719.plain: Brake Switch B Circuit Low: the signal voltage is below the expected range. Often a short to ground or high resistance in the wiring.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P071A.title: Transmission Mode Switch A Circuit
P071A.plain: Transmission Mode Switch A Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P071B.title: Transmission Mode Switch A Circuit Low
P071B.plain: Same as P071A with the signal shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P071C.title: Transmission Mode Switch A Circuit High
P071C.plain: Same as P071A with the signal shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P071D.title: Transmission Mode Switch B Circuit
P071D.plain: Transmission Mode Switch B Circuit: an electrical fault is present in the circuit.

P071E.title: Transmission Mode Switch B Circuit Low
P071E.plain: Same as P071B on switch B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P071F.title: Transmission Mode Switch B Circuit High
P071F.plain: Same as P071C on switch B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0720.title: Output Speed Sensor Circuit Malfunction
P0720.plain: The transmission output speed sensor signal is missing or implausible. The TCM uses this signal together with input speed to determine actual gear ratio; many vehicles also use it as a backup vehicle speed signal for the cluster and ECU.

P0721.title: Output Speed Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P0721.plain: The transmission output speed sensor signal is implausible compared to vehicle speed and gear ratio. Sometimes set together with VSS or input-speed-sensor codes.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0722.title: Output Speed Sensor Circuit No Signal
P0722.plain: TCM detects no output shaft speed signal while the vehicle is moving. Triggers shift abnormalities, speedometer issues, and limp-home mode.

P0723.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent
P0723.plain: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Intermittent: the signal is intermittent or erratic. Often a loose connector or chafed wiring; a wiggle test often locates it.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0724.title: Brake Switch B Circuit High
P0724.plain: Brake Switch B Circuit High: the signal voltage is above the expected range. Often an open circuit or a short to supply voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0725.title: Engine Speed Input Circuit
P0725.plain: A general circuit fault on the engine speed signal that the TCM receives from the ECM. Without this signal the TCM cannot synchronise gear shifts to engine load.
causes: Harness fault between ECM and TCM

P0726.title: Engine Speed Input Circuit Range or Performance
P0726.plain: Same as P0725 with the signal in plausible range yet not matching the engine model.
causes: Signal drift between ECM output and TCM input

P0727.title: Engine Speed Input Circuit No Signal
P0727.plain: The transmission control module receives no engine speed signal. Required to coordinate shifts and torque converter lockup with engine state.
causes: Speed signal lost on data bus

P0728.title: Engine Speed Input Circuit Intermittent
P0728.plain: Same as P0725 with intermittent or erratic signal. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0729.title: Gear 6 Incorrect Ratio
P0729.plain: When gear 6 is engaged, the measured ratio between the input- and output-shaft speed sensors does not match the expected ratio for that gear. This means the transmission is slipping in gear 6 rather than transmitting power solidly. Causes: worn clutch packs or bands, low fluid level or pressure, a stuck shift solenoid, or a valve-body fault affecting gear 6.

P072A.title: Stuck in Neutral
P072A.plain: The TCM detects that the transmission is mechanically stuck in neutral - shift solenoids do not engage a gear despite commanded driving range. Driveline produces no torque.

P072B.title: Stuck In Reverse
P072B.plain: Same as P072A with the transmission stuck in reverse - cannot select forward driving range.

P072C.title: Stuck in Gear 1
P072C.plain: The transmission is mechanically stuck in gear 1 and will not shift out of it. A shift solenoid or hydraulic valve on the gear-1 circuit has jammed, or a clutch/band has failed to release. Symptoms are no up- or downshifts, harsh behaviour, and often limp mode. Causes: a stuck or failed shift solenoid, a valve-body fault, a hydraulic pressure problem, or internal mechanical damage.
causes: Shift solenoid stuck in 1st gear position

P072D.title: Stuck in Gear 2
P072D.plain: The transmission is mechanically stuck in gear 2 and will not shift out of it. A shift solenoid or hydraulic valve on the gear-2 circuit has jammed, or a clutch/band has failed to release. Symptoms are no up- or downshifts, harsh behaviour, and often limp mode. Causes: a stuck or failed shift solenoid, a valve-body fault, a hydraulic pressure problem, or internal mechanical damage.

P072E.title: Stuck in Gear 3
P072E.plain: The transmission is mechanically stuck in gear 3 and will not shift out of it. A shift solenoid or hydraulic valve on the gear-3 circuit has jammed, or a clutch/band has failed to release. Symptoms are no up- or downshifts, harsh behaviour, and often limp mode. Causes: a stuck or failed shift solenoid, a valve-body fault, a hydraulic pressure problem, or internal mechanical damage.

P072F.title: Stuck in Gear 4
P072F.plain: The transmission is mechanically stuck in gear 4 and will not shift out of it. A shift solenoid or hydraulic valve on the gear-4 circuit has jammed, or a clutch/band has failed to release. Symptoms are no up- or downshifts, harsh behaviour, and often limp mode. Causes: a stuck or failed shift solenoid, a valve-body fault, a hydraulic pressure problem, or internal mechanical damage.

P0730.title: Incorrect Gear Ratio
P0730.plain: The ratio between input and output speed does not match any expected gear. Indicates slippage, valve body fault or sensor inaccuracy without identifying a specific gear.

P0731.title: Gear 1 Incorrect Ratio
P0731.plain: When gear 1 is engaged, the measured ratio between the input- and output-shaft speed sensors does not match the expected ratio for that gear. This means the transmission is slipping in gear 1 rather than transmitting power solidly. Causes: worn clutch packs or bands, low fluid level or pressure, a stuck shift solenoid, or a valve-body fault affecting gear 1.
causes: Line pressure low (pump or valve body)

P0732.title: Gear 2 Incorrect Ratio
P0732.plain: When gear 2 is engaged, the measured ratio between the input- and output-shaft speed sensors does not match the expected ratio for that gear. This means the transmission is slipping in gear 2 rather than transmitting power solidly. Causes: worn clutch packs or bands, low fluid level or pressure, a stuck shift solenoid, or a valve-body fault affecting gear 2.

P0733.title: Gear 3 Incorrect Ratio
P0733.plain: When gear 3 is engaged, the measured ratio between the input- and output-shaft speed sensors does not match the expected ratio for that gear. This means the transmission is slipping in gear 3 rather than transmitting power solidly. Causes: worn clutch packs or bands, low fluid level or pressure, a stuck shift solenoid, or a valve-body fault affecting gear 3.

P0734.title: Gear 4 Incorrect Ratio
P0734.plain: When gear 4 is engaged, the measured ratio between the input- and output-shaft speed sensors does not match the expected ratio for that gear. This means the transmission is slipping in gear 4 rather than transmitting power solidly. Causes: worn clutch packs or bands, low fluid level or pressure, a stuck shift solenoid, or a valve-body fault affecting gear 4.

P0735.title: Gear 5 Incorrect Ratio
P0735.plain: When gear 5 is engaged, the measured ratio between the input- and output-shaft speed sensors does not match the expected ratio for that gear. This means the transmission is slipping in gear 5 rather than transmitting power solidly. Causes: worn clutch packs or bands, low fluid level or pressure, a stuck shift solenoid, or a valve-body fault affecting gear 5.

P0736.title: Reverse Incorrect Ratio
P0736.plain: The TCM detected a ratio mismatch in reverse — likely a stuck solenoid, slipping clutch, or worn band.

P0737.title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit
P0737.plain: A circuit fault on the engine speed value the TCM sends to other modules (rev counter, hybrid module).

P0738.title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit Low
P0738.plain: Same as P0737 with the output shorted to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0739.title: TCM Engine Speed Output Circuit High
P0739.plain: Same as P0737 with the output shorted to supply. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P073A.title: Stuck in Gear 5
P073A.plain: The transmission is mechanically stuck in gear 5 and will not shift out of it. A shift solenoid or hydraulic valve on the gear-5 circuit has jammed, or a clutch/band has failed to release. Symptoms are no up- or downshifts, harsh behaviour, and often limp mode. Causes: a stuck or failed shift solenoid, a valve-body fault, a hydraulic pressure problem, or internal mechanical damage.

P073B.title: Stuck in Gear 6
P073B.plain: The transmission is mechanically stuck in gear 6 and will not shift out of it. A shift solenoid or hydraulic valve on the gear-6 circuit has jammed, or a clutch/band has failed to release. Symptoms are no up- or downshifts, harsh behaviour, and often limp mode. Causes: a stuck or failed shift solenoid, a valve-body fault, a hydraulic pressure problem, or internal mechanical damage.

P073C.title: Stuck in Gear 7
P073C.plain: The transmission is mechanically stuck in gear 7 and will not shift out of it. A shift solenoid or hydraulic valve on the gear-7 circuit has jammed, or a clutch/band has failed to release. Symptoms are no up- or downshifts, harsh behaviour, and often limp mode. Causes: a stuck or failed shift solenoid, a valve-body fault, a hydraulic pressure problem, or internal mechanical damage.

P073D.title: Unable to Engage Neutral
P073D.plain: The TCM cannot disengage all gears to neutral - typically a stuck clutch pack or hydraulic pressure issue keeping a gear engaged.

P073E.title: Unable to Engage Reverse
P073E.plain: Reverse cannot be engaged when commanded - reverse-band, clutch pack or hydraulic pressure on the reverse circuit has failed.

P073F.title: Unable to Engage Gear 1
P073F.plain: The transmission cannot engage gear 1 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 1 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in. Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-1 circuit.

P0740.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Malfunction
P0740.plain: A general fault has been detected in the torque converter clutch (TCC) lockup circuit. The TCC mechanically links the engine to the transmission input shaft above a certain speed to eliminate slip and improve fuel economy.

P0741.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Performance/Stuck Off
P0741.plain: When the TCM commands torque converter lockup, the actual slip stays above threshold — the clutch is not engaging. Often signals worn TCC friction material; transmission fluid analysis usually shows debris.
causes: TCC solenoid stuck or slow to react
Valve body wear (loss of clamping pressure)

P0742.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Stuck On
P0742.plain: The torque converter clutch (TCC) cannot disengage. Symptom is engine stalling when coming to a stop, because the engine is mechanically locked to the transmission output.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P0743.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Electrical
P0743.plain: An electrical fault in the torque converter clutch solenoid circuit — open, shorted, or out-of-range driver current. The transmission usually inhibits TCC apply when this code is active.

P0744.title: Torque Converter Clutch Circuit Intermittent
P0744.plain: The TCC circuit drops in and out — intermittent open or short. Symptoms include erratic shudder at lock-up speeds and intermittent engine stalls when stopping.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0745.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A
P0745.plain: A general fault on transmission pressure control solenoid A - the solenoid that meters main line pressure for the entire valve body.

P0746.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Performance
P0746.plain: Pressure Control Solenoid A Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. It regulates transmission line pressure; faults cause slipping, harsh, or delayed shifts.

P0747.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Stuck On
P0747.plain: Pressure control solenoid A appears electrically commanded off but pressure feedback indicates it is stuck on. Line pressure stays high.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P0748.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Electrical
P0748.plain: An electrical fault on the pressure control solenoid A circuit - typically open or short to ground or supply.

P0749.title: Pressure Control Solenoid A Intermittent
P0749.plain: Same as P0748 with intermittent or erratic signal.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P074A.title: Unable to Engage Gear 2
P074A.plain: The transmission cannot engage gear 2 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 2 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in. Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-2 circuit.

P074B.title: Unable to Engage Gear 3
P074B.plain: The transmission cannot engage gear 3 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 3 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in.
