Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-3 circuit.

P074C.title: Unable to Engage Gear 4
P074C.plain: The transmission cannot engage gear 4 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 4 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in. Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-4 circuit.

P074D.title: Unable to Engage Gear 5
P074D.plain: The transmission cannot engage gear 5 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 5 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in. Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-5 circuit.

P074E.title: Unable to Engage Gear 6
P074E.plain: The transmission cannot engage gear 6 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 6 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in. Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-6 circuit.

P074F.title: Unable to Engage Gear 7
P074F.plain: The transmission cannot engage gear 7 when it is commanded. The element that should apply for gear 7 — shift solenoid, clutch pack, or band — does not build or hold pressure, so the gear never locks in. Symptoms are slipping, no power transfer in that gear, or a forced limp mode. Causes: a failed shift solenoid, a worn clutch pack, or a valve-body or hydraulic-supply fault on the gear-7 circuit.

P0750.title: Shift Solenoid "A" Malfunction
P0750.plain: Shift Solenoid "A" Malfunction: the component is malfunctioning. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.

P0751.title: Shift Solenoid A Performance
P0751.plain: Shift Solenoid A Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.

P0752.title: Shift Solenoid A Stuck On
P0752.plain: Shift Solenoid A Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P0753.title: Shift Solenoid A Electrical
P0753.plain: An electrical fault on shift solenoid A - open or short on the control circuit.

P0754.title: Shift Solenoid A Intermittent
P0754.plain: Same as P0753 with intermittent signal.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0755.title: Shift Solenoid "B" Malfunction
P0755.plain: Shift Solenoid "B" Malfunction: the component is malfunctioning. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.

P0756.title: Shift Solenoid B Performance
P0756.plain: Shift Solenoid B Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.

P0757.title: Shift Solenoid B Stuck On
P0757.plain: Shift Solenoid B Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P0758.title: Shift Solenoid "B" Electrical
P0758.plain: Shift Solenoid "B" Electrical: an electrical fault is present. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.

P0759.title: Shift Solenoid B Intermittent
P0759.plain: Same as P0754 on shift solenoid B.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P075A.title: Shift Solenoid G
P075A.plain: A general fault on shift solenoid G - typically the seventh shift solenoid in transmissions with 7 or more gears.

P075B.title: Shift Solenoid G Performance/Stuck Off
P075B.plain: Shift solenoid G is electrically intact, but its hydraulic effect is missing — when commanded on, the gear it should engage does not lock up. Either the solenoid is mechanically stuck closed, the valve body bore is worn, or hydraulic pressure does not reach the clutch pack.
causes: Solenoid stuck closed by debris in the ATF
Worn valve body bore leaking pressure

P075C.title: Shift Solenoid G Stuck On
P075C.plain: Shift solenoid G remains hydraulically active even when the TCM commands it off. The corresponding clutch or band stays applied, blocking shifts that need it released — typical symptoms are harsh engagement, stuck in a single gear, or refusal to shift cleanly.
causes: Stuck valve spool in the valve body
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P075D.title: Shift Solenoid G Electrical
P075D.plain: General electrical fault on the shift solenoid G control circuit — open coil, short to ground, short to battery voltage, or driver feedback outside the expected range. The TCM disables this solenoid and falls back to limp-home gear logic to protect the transmission.
causes: Damaged wiring at the transmission case connector

P075E.title: Shift Solenoid G Intermittent
P075E.plain: Shift solenoid G shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts — vibration on the harness, loose connector, contaminated ATF that occasionally jams the spool, or thermal sensitivity. Difficult to catch with a static check; usually documented by snapshot/freeze-frame data when the fault occurs.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P075F.title: Transmission Fluid Level Too High
P075F.plain: The transmission fluid level monitor reports overfill above the safe maximum. Causes range from incorrect refill at service to coolant intrusion via a failed transmission cooler. Overfilling can cause foaming, accelerated wear and seal damage from raised internal pressure.
causes: Coolant intrusion through a failed transmission cooler

P0760.title: Shift Solenoid "C" Malfunction
P0760.plain: Shift Solenoid "C" Malfunction: the component is malfunctioning. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.

P0761.title: Shift Solenoid C Performance
P0761.plain: Shift Solenoid C Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.

P0762.title: Shift Solenoid C Stuck On
P0762.plain: Shift solenoid C remains hydraulically active when commanded off — the corresponding clutch or band cannot release, locking out shifts that depend on it. The TCM detects the missing release via gear-ratio error or output-shaft slip.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P0763.title: Shift Solenoid "C" Electrical
P0763.plain: Shift Solenoid "C" Electrical: an electrical fault is present. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.

P0764.title: Shift Solenoid C Intermittent
P0764.plain: Shift solenoid C shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts — vibration, loose connector, ATF contamination or thermal sensitivity. Hard to reproduce on a static bench check.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0765.title: Shift Solenoid "D" Malfunction
P0765.plain: Shift Solenoid "D" Malfunction: the component is malfunctioning. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.

P0766.title: Shift Solenoid D Performance
P0766.plain: Shift Solenoid D Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.

P0767.title: Shift Solenoid D Stuck On
P0767.plain: Shift solenoid D remains hydraulically active when commanded off — corresponding clutch or band cannot release. The TCM detects the missing release via gear-ratio error.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P0768.title: Shift Solenoid "D" Electrical
P0768.plain: Shift Solenoid "D" Electrical: an electrical fault is present. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.

P0769.title: Shift Solenoid D Intermittent
P0769.plain: Shift solenoid D shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P076A.title: Shift Solenoid H
P076A.plain: General fault on shift solenoid H — used in 8/9/10-speed transmissions where multiple shift solenoids manage the larger gear matrix. The TCM detects an electrical or hydraulic anomaly without yet being able to attribute it to a specific failure mode.

P076B.title: Shift Solenoid H Performance/Stuck Off
P076B.plain: Shift solenoid H is electrically intact but does not engage hydraulically when commanded — corresponding clutch or band does not lock up.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P076C.title: Shift Solenoid H Stuck On
P076C.plain: Shift solenoid H remains hydraulically active when commanded off — corresponding clutch or band cannot release, blocking dependent shifts.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P076D.title: Shift Solenoid H Electrical
P076D.plain: General electrical fault on the shift solenoid H control circuit — open coil, short to ground or battery, driver feedback outside range.
causes: Damaged wiring at the transmission connector

P076E.title: Shift Solenoid H Intermittent
P076E.plain: Shift solenoid H shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P076F.title: Gear 7 Incorrect Ratio
P076F.plain: While in 7th gear, the ratio measured between input shaft speed and output shaft speed does not match the calibrated value for that gear. Either a clutch or band is slipping, the wrong gear actually engaged, or speed sensor data is wrong.
causes: Wrong shift solenoid pattern engaging the wrong gear

P0770.title: Shift Solenoid E
P0770.plain: General fault on shift solenoid E. The TCM detects an electrical or hydraulic anomaly that has not yet been pinned to a specific failure mode.

P0771.title: Shift Solenoid E Performance/Stuck Off
P0771.plain: Shift solenoid E is electrically intact but does not engage hydraulically — associated clutch or band does not lock up.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P0772.title: Shift Solenoid E Stuck On
P0772.plain: Shift solenoid E remains hydraulically active when commanded off — associated clutch or band cannot release, blocking dependent shifts.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P0773.title: Shift Solenoid "E" Electrical
P0773.plain: Shift Solenoid "E" Electrical: an electrical fault is present. Shift solenoids route transmission hydraulic pressure to engage the gears; faults cause harsh, delayed, or missed shifts.

P0774.title: Shift Solenoid E Intermittent
P0774.plain: Shift solenoid E shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts — vibration, loose connector or ATF contamination.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0775.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B
P0775.plain: Generic fault on pressure control solenoid B circuit. Either electrical or response fault depending on manufacturer.

P0776.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Performance
P0776.plain: Pressure Control Solenoid B Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. It regulates transmission line pressure; faults cause slipping, harsh, or delayed shifts.

P0777.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Stuck On
P0777.plain: Pressure control solenoid B does not release line pressure when commanded — output pressure remains at maximum, leading to harsh shifts and elevated stress on the clutch packs and seals.
causes: Contaminated ATF clogging the pressure control valve
Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P0778.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Electrical
P0778.plain: General electrical fault on the pressure control solenoid B circuit — open coil, short to ground or battery, or driver feedback outside the expected range.
causes: Damaged wiring at the transmission case connector

P0779.title: Pressure Control Solenoid B Intermittent
P0779.plain: Pressure control solenoid B shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts — vibration, loose connector, or contaminated ATF that occasionally restricts the regulator port.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P077A.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit - Loss of Direction Signal
P077A.plain: The output shaft speed sensor uses a quadrature output (two channels phase-shifted by 90°) so the TCM can determine direction of rotation. The direction channel is missing — TCM cannot tell whether the vehicle is rolling forward or backward, blocking neutral-idle and rollback-protection strategies.

P077B.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit - Direction Error
P077B.plain: The TCM reads a direction from the output shaft speed sensor that contradicts the commanded gear — for example reverse direction while drive is engaged, or forward direction while reverse is engaged. Either the sensor wiring is swapped, the sensor is wrong, or the gear actually engaged is not the one commanded.

P077C.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit Low
P077C.plain: Output shaft speed sensor signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open supply. TCM disables vehicle-speed dependent shift logic and may force limp-home.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P077D.title: Output Shaft Speed Sensor Circuit High
P077D.plain: Output shaft speed sensor signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.
causes: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P077E.title: Transmission Fluid Temperature Measurement System - Multiple Sensor Correlation
P077E.plain: Modern transmissions can have two or more ATF temperature sensors (sump, cooler return, valve body). After a long key-off soak they should all read approximately the same ambient. The TCM detects an implausible spread between sensors — one of them drifts or is wired wrong.

P077F.title: Reverse 2 Incorrect Ratio
P077F.plain: Some transmissions provide a second reverse ratio (typically a slower crawler reverse for trailer manoeuvring or hill descent). The TCM detects that the input/output ratio in this gear does not match its calibrated value — slipping clutch or wrong gear actually engaged.

P0780.title: Shift Malfunction
P0780.plain: The TCM detects that a commanded shift between gears did not occur within the expected time and quality window. Slip rates or speed ratios remain implausible during shift.

P0781.title: 1-2 Shift Malfunction
P0781.plain: The TCM detects a fault during the 1-to-2 upshift. The actual gear ratio after the shift command does not match the expected ratio for second gear.

P0782.title: 2-3 Shift Malfunction
P0782.plain: The TCM detects a fault during the 2-to-3 upshift. Gear ratio after shift command does not match third gear expected ratio.

P0783.title: 3-4 Shift Malfunction
P0783.plain: The TCM detects a fault during the 3-to-4 upshift, where gear ratio after the shift does not match fourth gear expected value.

P0784.title: 4-5 Shift Malfunction
P0784.plain: The TCM detects a fault during the 4-to-5 upshift on transmissions equipped with five or more forward gears.

P0785.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A
P0785.plain: General fault on shift timing solenoid A — controls the rate at which a shift event takes place (smooth ramp vs. quick snap). The TCM detects an electrical or hydraulic anomaly that has not yet been pinned to a specific failure mode.

P0786.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A Range/Performance
P0786.plain: Shift timing solenoid A is electrically intact, but the actual shift time does not match the model — shifts too fast (harsh) or too slow (slipping under load). Often aged solenoid with weakened force or contaminated ATF restricting the regulating port.
causes: Aged solenoid with weakened magnetic force
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0787.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A Low
P0787.plain: Shift timing solenoid A control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on.

P0788.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A High
P0788.plain: Shift timing solenoid A control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil/return.
causes: Control wire shorted to battery voltage

P0789.title: Shift Timing Solenoid A Intermittent
P0789.plain: Shift timing solenoid A signal jumps or drops out — vibration, loose connector or thermal sensitivity.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P078A.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B
P078A.plain: General fault on shift timing solenoid B — second timing solenoid for shift events that need a different ramp profile (typically downshifts vs. upshifts, or specific gear pairs).

P078B.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B Range/Performance
P078B.plain: Shift timing solenoid B is electrically intact, but actual shift timing does not match the model — same failure modes as solenoid A (aged, dirty ATF), applied to the second timing channel.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P078C.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B Low
P078C.plain: Shift timing solenoid B control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground.

P078D.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B High
P078D.plain: Shift timing solenoid B control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil.
causes: Control wire shorted to battery voltage

P078E.title: Shift Timing Solenoid B Intermittent
P078E.plain: Shift timing solenoid B signal jumps or drops out.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P078F.title: Transmission Mode Switch C Circuit
P078F.plain: General electrical fault on the third transmission mode select switch input C — used for additional drive modes (Sport, Snow, Tow/Haul, Eco) on transmissions that offer more than two operator-selectable shift maps. Without a valid input the TCM falls back to the default mode.

P0790.title: Normal/Performance Switch Circuit
P0790.plain: General electrical fault on the Normal/Performance shift-pattern selector switch — lets the driver toggle between a comfort-oriented and a sport-oriented shift map. Without a valid input the TCM defaults to the Normal map.

P0791.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit
P0791.plain: The TCM detects an electrical fault on the intermediate shaft speed sensor A circuit. Used to compute shift slip and torque converter behavior.

P0792.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0792.plain: The intermediate shaft speed sensor (between input and output, used in CVT and dual-clutch boxes for slip detection between gear elements) is electrically intact, but its readings drift away from the model. The TCM cannot reliably detect slip in this stage.
causes: Aged Hall element with reduced amplitude
Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0793.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit No Signal
P0793.plain: Intermediate shaft speed sensor A is connected and powered, but no rotation pulses arrive while the transmission is in motion. Either the sensor reluctor wheel is damaged, the sensor air gap is wrong, or the element has failed open.

P0794.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0794.plain: Intermediate shaft speed sensor A signal jumps or drops out — vibration, loose connector or oil mist on the sensor tip.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0795.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C
P0795.plain: General fault on pressure control solenoid C — third pressure regulator in transmissions with multiple independently regulated hydraulic circuits (line pressure, clutch C, torque converter clutch). The TCM detects an electrical or hydraulic anomaly that has not yet been pinned to a specific failure mode.

P0796.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Performance
P0796.plain: Pressure Control Solenoid C Performance: the component is electrically intact but its response does not match the command. It regulates transmission line pressure; faults cause slipping, harsh, or delayed shifts.

P0797.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Stuck On
P0797.plain: The TCM detects that pressure control solenoid C remains energized hydraulically despite commanded de-energization. Line pressure or shift quality deviates from target.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P0798.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Electrical
P0798.plain: The TCM detects an electrical fault in the pressure control solenoid C circuit, such as open winding, short to ground or short to power.

P0799.title: Pressure Control Solenoid C Intermittent
P0799.plain: Pressure control solenoid C shows intermittent electrical or hydraulic dropouts.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P079A.title: Transmission Friction Element A Slip Detected
P079A.plain: Friction element A (the first clutch or band in the gear matrix) shows measurable slip while it should be fully engaged. Detected by comparing input/output speed sensors against the commanded gear ratio. Slip means the element cannot transmit full torque — risk of glazing the friction surfaces.
causes: Worn friction discs in element A
Low hydraulic pressure to element A

P079B.title: Transmission Friction Element B Slip Detected
P079B.plain: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element B (the second clutch or band).
causes: Worn friction discs in element B

P079C.title: Transmission Friction Element C Slip Detected
P079C.plain: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element C (third clutch or band).
causes: Worn friction discs in element C

P079D.title: Transmission Friction Element D Slip Detected
P079D.plain: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element D (fourth clutch or band).
causes: Worn friction discs in element D

P079E.title: Transmission Friction Element E Slip Detected
P079E.plain: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element E (fifth clutch or band, used in 8/9/10-speed transmissions).
causes: Worn friction discs in element E

P079F.title: Transmission Friction Element F Slip Detected
P079F.plain: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element F (sixth clutch or band, used in 8/9/10-speed transmissions).
causes: Worn friction discs in element F

P07A0.title: Transmission Friction Element G Slip Detected
P07A0.plain: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element G (seventh clutch or band, used in 9/10-speed transmissions).
causes: Worn friction discs in element G

P07A1.title: Transmission Friction Element H Slip Detected
P07A1.plain: Same condition as element A slip, applied to friction element H (eighth clutch or band, in 10-speed transmissions).
causes: Worn friction discs in element H

P07A2.title: Transmission Friction Element A Performance/Stuck Off
P07A2.plain: Friction element A does not lock up when commanded — its hydraulic circuit cannot bring the clutch pack into full engagement. Either the apply piston is stuck, the seal is leaking past the piston, or the supplying pressure regulator is failing.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P07A3.title: Transmission Friction Element A Stuck On
P07A3.plain: Friction element A does not release when commanded — the apply piston cannot retract, leaving the clutch or band engaged. The transmission cannot complete shifts that need element A released, leading to harsh engagement or stall when stopping.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement

P07A4.title: Transmission Friction Element B Performance/Stuck Off
P07A4.plain: Transmission Friction Element B Performance/Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07A5.title: Transmission Friction Element B Stuck On
P07A5.plain: Transmission Friction Element B Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07A6.title: Transmission Friction Element C Performance/Stuck Off
P07A6.plain: Transmission Friction Element C Performance/Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07A7.title: Transmission Friction Element C Stuck On
P07A7.plain: Transmission Friction Element C Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07A8.title: Transmission Friction Element D Performance/Stuck Off
P07A8.plain: Transmission Friction Element D Performance/Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07A9.title: Transmission Friction Element D Stuck On
P07A9.plain: Transmission Friction Element D Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07AA.title: Transmission Friction Element E Performance/Stuck Off
P07AA.plain: Transmission Friction Element E Performance/Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07AB.title: Transmission Friction Element E Stuck On
P07AB.plain: Transmission Friction Element E Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07AC.title: Transmission Friction Element F Performance/Stuck Off
P07AC.plain: Transmission Friction Element F Performance/Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07AD.title: Transmission Friction Element F Stuck On
P07AD.plain: Transmission Friction Element F Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07AE.title: Transmission Friction Element G Performance/Stuck Off
P07AE.plain: Transmission Friction Element G Performance/Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07AF.title: Transmission Friction Element G Stuck On
P07AF.plain: Transmission Friction Element G Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07B0.title: Transmission Friction Element H Performance/Stuck Off
P07B0.plain: Transmission Friction Element H Performance/Stuck Off: the actuator is stuck in the off position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07B1.title: Transmission Friction Element H Stuck On
P07B1.plain: Transmission Friction Element H Stuck On: the actuator is stuck in the on position.
causes: Carbon or debris buildup preventing free movement
Component wear with age - mechanical play

P07B2.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit/Open
P07B2.plain: Park position sensor/switch A — confirms that the gear selector lever is in Park, used by shift-by-wire systems and key-interlock logic — is open. The TCM cannot confirm Park engagement, blocking key removal and engine restart logic.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P07B3.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Low
P07B3.plain: Park position sensor/switch A reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07B4.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit High
P07B4.plain: Park position sensor/switch A reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open switch return. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07B5.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Performance/Low
P07B5.plain: Sensor A is electrically intact but its low-end value drifts — for example a value below the calibrated Park threshold while the lever is mechanically out of Park. The TCM cannot fully trust the Park reading.
causes: Aged Hall element with offset drift

P07B6.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Performance High
P07B6.plain: Sensor A is electrically intact but the high-end value drifts — for example a value above the calibrated non-Park range while the lever actually is in Park.

P07B7.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P07B7.plain: Park position sensor A signal jumps or drops out — typically a worn switch with contact bounce or a loose connector at the shift lever module.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P07B8.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit/Open
P07B8.plain: Park position sensor/switch B is the redundant/secondary park-confirmation sensor — used in shift-by-wire systems for safety, so a single sensor failure cannot strand the vehicle in Park or hide a non-Park condition. With B open the TCM falls back to sensor A only.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P07B9.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Low
P07B9.plain: Park sensor/switch B reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07BA.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit High
P07BA.plain: Park sensor/switch B reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07BB.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Performance/Low
P07BB.plain: Sensor B low-end value drifts away from the calibrated Park threshold.

P07BC.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Performance High
P07BC.plain: Sensor B high-end value drifts above the calibrated non-Park range.

P07BD.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch B Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P07BD.plain: Sensor B signal jumps or drops out. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P07BE.title: Transmission Park Position Sensor/Switch A/B Correlation
P07BE.plain: The two redundant park position sensors A and B disagree — one reports Park, the other does not. Until the discrepancy is cleared the TCM cannot trust either reading and falls back to a safe state (typically blocking key removal and engine restart).
causes: One of the two sensors drifting outside tolerance

P07BF.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P07BF.plain: Input/turbine shaft speed sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open supply. Without this signal the TCM cannot calculate slip across the torque converter or first gear element.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07C0.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit High
P07C0.plain: Sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07C1.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit Low
P07C1.plain: Same as sensor A circuit low, applied to sensor B (used in dual-clutch boxes for the second input shaft). Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07C2.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit High
P07C2.plain: Same as sensor A circuit high, applied to sensor B. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07C3.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit Low
P07C3.plain: Same as sensor A circuit low, applied to sensor C (used in some heavy-duty or hybrid-coupled transmissions with three input speed sensors).
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07C4.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit High
P07C4.plain: Same as sensor A circuit high, applied to sensor C. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07C5.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit Low
P07C5.plain: Intermediate shaft speed sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07C6.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor A Circuit High
P07C6.plain: Intermediate shaft speed sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07C7.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit Low
P07C7.plain: Intermediate shaft speed sensor B (second intermediate sensor in dual-clutch boxes) signal voltage below the lower limit.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07C8.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor B Circuit High
P07C8.plain: Intermediate shaft speed sensor B signal voltage above the upper limit. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07C9.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit Low
P07C9.plain: Intermediate shaft speed sensor C (third intermediate sensor in heavy-duty or hybrid-coupled transmissions) signal voltage below the lower limit.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07CA.title: Intermediate Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit High
P07CA.plain: Intermediate shaft speed sensor C signal voltage above the upper limit. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07CB.title: Transmission Fluid Thermostat Performance
P07CB.plain: The transmission fluid thermostat (similar in function to a coolant thermostat — opens at a calibrated temperature to route ATF through the cooler) does not regulate temperature within the expected band. Either stuck open (ATF stays cold, friction modifier ineffective) or stuck closed (ATF overheats, oxidising the fluid).

P07CC.title: Transmission Mode Switch C Circuit Low
P07CC.plain: Transmission mode switch C input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07CD.title: Transmission Mode Switch C Circuit High
P07CD.plain: Transmission mode switch C input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07CE.title: Transmission Mode Switch D Circuit
P07CE.plain: General electrical fault on the fourth transmission mode select switch input D — additional drive mode beyond C (e.g. Manumatic, Off-Road, Trailer).

P07CF.title: Transmission Mode Switch D Circuit Low
P07CF.plain: Mode switch D input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07D0.title: Transmission Mode Switch D Circuit High
P07D0.plain: Mode switch D input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07D1.title: Transmission Mode Switch E Circuit
P07D1.plain: General electrical fault on the fifth transmission mode select switch input E.

P07D2.title: Transmission Mode Switch E Circuit Low
P07D2.plain: Mode switch E input reads stuck low. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07D3.title: Transmission Mode Switch E Circuit High
P07D3.plain: Mode switch E input reads stuck high. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07D4.title: Transmission Mode Switch F Circuit
P07D4.plain: General electrical fault on the sixth transmission mode select switch input F.

P07D5.title: Transmission Mode Switch F Circuit Low
P07D5.plain: Mode switch F input reads stuck low. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07D6.title: Transmission Mode Switch F Circuit High
P07D6.plain: Mode switch F input reads stuck high. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07D7.title: Stuck in Gear 8
P07D7.plain: The transmission has entered 8th gear but cannot leave it on command — typically a stuck shift solenoid or a stuck-on friction element holding the 8th-gear pattern locked. The TCM forces limp-home mode if upshift/downshift attempts fail repeatedly.

P07D8.title: Unable To Engage Gear 8
P07D8.plain: The TCM commands a shift to 8th gear but the gear-ratio measurement does not confirm engagement — friction element does not lock up, slipping clutch, or shift solenoid does not respond. Falls back to the previously engaged gear.

P07D9.title: Gear 8 Incorrect Ratio
P07D9.plain: While in 8th gear, the measured input/output ratio does not match the calibrated value — slipping clutch, wrong gear actually engaged, or speed sensor data wrong.

P07DA.title: 6-7 Shift
P07DA.plain: General fault detected during the 6-to-7 upshift event — slipping during the shift, gear-ratio overshoot, or shift completion timeout. Often a worn friction element on the 7th-gear side or a slow shift solenoid.

P07DB.title: 7-8 Shift
P07DB.plain: General fault detected during the 7-to-8 upshift event.

P07DC.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 1
P07DC.plain: Starting from 1st gear, the TCM commanded a specific upshift but the resulting gear ratio matches a different gear. Wrong shift solenoid pattern actually engaged, or a stuck solenoid blocked the intended pattern.

P07DD.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 2
P07DD.plain: Same condition as incorrect shift from gear 1, applied to shifts originating in 2nd gear.

P07DE.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 3
P07DE.plain: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 3rd gear.

P07DF.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 4
P07DF.plain: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 4th gear.

P07E0.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 5
P07E0.plain: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 5th gear.

P07E1.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 6
P07E1.plain: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 6th gear.

P07E2.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 7
P07E2.plain: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 7th gear.

P07E3.title: Incorrect Shift from Gear 8
P07E3.plain: Same condition, applied to shifts originating in 8th gear.

P07E4.title: Unable to Engage Park
P07E4.plain: The TCM commands the park pawl to engage but the position sensors do not confirm engagement — typical for shift-by-wire systems where the park actuator (motor or solenoid driving the pawl) is faulty, the cable is broken, or the pawl is jammed against a tooth and cannot drop in.
causes: Park pawl jammed against tooth (rock vehicle to release)

P07E5.title: Unable to Engage Drive
P07E5.plain: TCM commands engagement of Drive but the input/output speed relationship does not match — friction element does not lock up, or the shift solenoid pattern for Drive cannot be commanded. Vehicle remains stuck in Park or Neutral.

P07E6.title: Stuck in Park
P07E6.plain: The vehicle cannot leave Park even though the operator has commanded a different range. Park pawl jammed, park actuator failed, or shift-by-wire input not received by TCM.

P07E7.title: Stuck in Drive
P07E7.plain: The vehicle cannot leave Drive — typically a stuck shift mechanism, a stuck-on friction element, or a TCM that cannot command the shift to Park or Neutral.

P07E8.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit/Open
P07E8.plain: The transmission range control A circuit (used in shift-by-wire to drive the shift actuator that physically positions the manual valve in the valve body) is open. The TCM cannot move the manual valve into the commanded range, blocking shifts between P/R/N/D.
causes: Open wire to the range actuator
Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P07E9.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit Performance
P07E9.plain: Range control A circuit is electrically intact, but the actuator response does not match the model — for example position feedback that does not move when commanded, or moves slower than expected. Often a sticking actuator or aged motor.

P07EA.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit Low
P07EA.plain: Range control A circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07EB.title: Transmission Range Control A Circuit High
P07EB.plain: Range control A circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil/return. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07EC.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit
P07EC.plain: General electrical fault on the multi-function transmission range select circuit — used on shift-by-wire systems with rotary or push-button selectors that encode P/R/N/D as a multi-bit pattern. With the input invalid the TCM cannot decode the operator request.

P07ED.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Stuck
P07ED.plain: The multi-function select circuit reports a value that does not change despite operator activity — the rotary encoder is stuck or a push-button is mechanically locked. The TCM ignores further requests until the input becomes plausible.

P07EE.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Range/Performance
P07EE.plain: The multi-function select circuit produces values that do not match any valid bit pattern — multiple positions asserted simultaneously, or values outside the calibrated range.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P07EF.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit Low
P07EF.plain: Multi-function select circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or pegged at minimum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P07F0.title: Transmission Range Multi-Function Select Circuit High
P07F0.plain: Multi-function select circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or pegged at maximum. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P07F1.title: Input/Turbine Shaft Speed Sensor C Circuit
P07F1.plain: General electrical fault on input/turbine speed sensor C — third input speed sensor in heavy-duty or hybrid-coupled transmissions.

P07F2.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit
P07F2.plain: General fault on the communication line between the TCM and a separate transmission range control module (used on systems where the rotary/push-button selector lives in its own intelligent module that talks to the TCM via CAN or LIN).
causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly

P07F3.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit Low
P07F3.plain: Range control module communication line reads stuck low — bus shorted to ground or one node held the line low continuously.
causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P07F4.title: Transmission Range Control Module Communication Circuit High
P07F4.plain: Range control module communication line reads stuck high — bus shorted to battery voltage or open at the bus terminator.
causes: Gateway module routing CAN messages incorrectly
CAN terminating resistor (120 Ω) drifted out of spec

P07F5.title: Transmission Range Control Module System Voltage Low
P07F5.plain: The range control module reports its supply voltage below the operating threshold — vehicle battery low, charging system underperforming, or supply line resistance excessive. The module may stop responding until voltage recovers.

P07F6.title: Gear 9 Incorrect Ratio
P07F6.plain: While in 9th gear, the measured input/output ratio does not match the calibrated value — slipping clutch, wrong gear actually engaged, or speed sensor data wrong.

P07F7.title: Gear 10 Incorrect Ratio
P07F7.plain: While in 10th gear, the measured input/output ratio does not match the calibrated value.

P07F8.title: Stuck in Gear 9
P07F8.plain: Same condition as stuck in 8th gear, applied to 9th.

P07F9.title: Unable to Engage Gear 9
P07F9.plain: Same condition as unable to engage 8th gear, applied to 9th.

P07FA.title: Incorrect Shift From Gear 9
P07FA.plain: Same condition as incorrect shift from 8th, applied to 9th.

P07FB.title: Stuck in Gear 10
P07FB.plain: Same condition as stuck in 8th, applied to 10th.

P07FC.title: Unable to Engage Gear 10
P07FC.plain: Same condition as unable to engage 8th, applied to 10th.

P07FD.title: Incorrect Shift From Gear 10
P07FD.plain: Same condition as incorrect shift from 8th, applied to 10th.

P07FE.title: Stuck In Gear - Not Specified
P07FE.plain: The TCM detects that the transmission is stuck in some gear but cannot identify which one — typically because multiple input/output ratio cross-checks fail simultaneously, or an early-detection diagnostic fires before the specific-gear detection runs.

P07FF.title: Cold Start Transmission Performance
P07FF.plain: During the cold-start phase the transmission does not behave to specification — typically very slow shifts, missed shifts or harsh engagement at low ATF temperature. Common causes are degraded ATF (lost cold-flow viscosity), a stuck thermostat or aged solenoid drivers.

P0800.title: Transfer Case Control System (MIL Request)
P0800.plain: The transfer case control module has requested the ECM/PCM to illuminate the MIL because of a fault on its side that is emissions- or driveline-relevant. The original fault is in the transfer case module itself.
causes: Internal fault in transfer case module — read its DTCs

P0801.title: Reverse Inhibit Control Circuit
P0801.plain: The TCM detects an electrical fault in the reverse inhibit solenoid circuit, which prevents engagement of reverse at high vehicle speeds.

P0802.title: Transmission Control System MIL Request Circuit/Open
P0802.plain: The dedicated MIL request line from the TCM to the ECM (used in older systems where modules used a hard wire to ask for the MIL instead of CAN messaging) is open. The ECM cannot honour TCM-side MIL requests.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0803.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit
P0803.plain: General electrical fault on the upshift/skip-shift solenoid control circuit — used on manual-transmission performance vehicles to force a skip from 1st straight to 4th under low-load cruise (CAFE fuel-economy feature). With the input invalid the lockout cannot be applied.

P0804.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Lamp Control Circuit
P0804.plain: General electrical fault on the upshift/skip-shift indicator lamp control circuit — the dashboard light that prompts the driver to skip from 1st straight to 4th. With the input invalid the lamp cannot be illuminated.

P0805.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit
P0805.plain: General electrical fault on the clutch position sensor A circuit — used in dual-clutch and automated-manual transmissions to monitor clutch fork or release-bearing position. Without a valid signal the TCM cannot close the loop on clutch engagement.

P0806.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P0806.plain: Clutch position sensor A is electrically intact, but its readings drift away from the model — for example the position does not move when the actuator is commanded, or the offset shifts after a thermal cycle. Often a misadjusted sensor mount.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P0807.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Low
P0807.plain: Clutch position sensor A signal voltage below the lower limit — short to ground or open reference voltage.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0808.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit High
P0808.plain: Clutch position sensor A signal voltage above the upper limit — short to reference voltage or open signal return.
causes: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0809.title: Clutch Position Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P0809.plain: Clutch position sensor A signal jumps or drops out — vibration, loose connector or oil/heat exposure near the bell housing.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P080A.title: Clutch Position Not Learned
P080A.plain: After a clutch replacement or sensor replacement the TCM has not run a successful clutch-position learn cycle. Without learned end-stops the TCM cannot accurately command engagement points, leading to slipping or harsh take-up. A scan-tool guided learn procedure must be performed.
causes: Learn cycle not performed after service

P080B.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Range/Performance
P080B.plain: Skip-shift solenoid is electrically intact, but the lockout effect does not match commands — solenoid sticks or coil aged, gearbox interlock cannot be applied or released within the expected time.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P080C.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit Low
P080C.plain: Skip-shift solenoid control circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P080D.title: Upshift/Skip Shift Solenoid Control Circuit High
P080D.plain: Skip-shift solenoid control circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage or open coil. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Control wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0810.title: Clutch Position Control Error
P0810.plain: On automated manual or dual-clutch transmissions, the actual clutch actuator position deviates from commanded position beyond tolerance. Position sensor and actuator do not agree on closed-loop test.

P0811.title: Excessive Clutch A Slippage
P0811.plain: The TCM detects more slip across clutch A (the first clutch in dual-clutch boxes, or the launch clutch in automated-manual systems) than the calibration allows. Heat builds up rapidly — risk of glazing the friction discs or warping the pressure plate.
causes: Low clamp force from aged actuator

P0812.title: Reverse Input Circuit
P0812.plain: General electrical fault on the reverse-engagement input — the signal that tells the TCM (and other modules — backup lights, parking sensors) that the gear lever is in Reverse. With the input invalid backup lights and rear sensors do not activate.
causes: Open or shorted reverse input wire

P0813.title: Reverse Output Circuit
P0813.plain: General electrical fault on the reverse-output circuit — the line that drives backup lights, reverse alarm or transfer-case reverse signal. With the output broken these consumers cannot be activated.

P0814.title: Transmission Range Display Circuit
P0814.plain: General electrical fault on the transmission range display circuit — drives the PRNDL indicator on the dashboard. With the input invalid the indicator may show the wrong gear range or stay blank.

P0815.title: Upshift Switch Circuit
P0815.plain: The TCM detects an electrical fault on the manual upshift request switch (paddle or +/- lever) circuit.

P0816.title: Downshift Switch Circuit
P0816.plain: The TCM detects an electrical fault on the manual downshift request switch circuit.

P0817.title: Starter Disable Circuit/Open
P0817.plain: The starter-disable circuit (used by transmission, immobiliser or anti-theft to block cranking unless safety conditions are met — e.g. clutch pedal pressed on manual, brake pedal on auto) is open. The starter cannot be disabled, weakening the safety chain.
causes: Pin pushed back out of connector body
Cracked solder joint inside the module or sensor

P0818.title: Driveline Disconnect Switch Input Circuit
P0818.plain: General electrical fault on the driveline disconnect switch input — used on AWD/4WD vehicles to electrically disengage the rear or front axle for fuel economy. With the input invalid the disconnect cannot be commanded.

P0819.title: Up and Down Shift Switch to Transmission Range Correlation
P0819.plain: The up-shift/down-shift paddle or button input is used in manumatic mode to step through gears, but the inputs only make sense when the gear lever is in Drive or the Manual position. The TCM detects an inconsistency — paddle commands while gear lever is in Park or Neutral.

P081A.title: Starter Disable Circuit Low
P081A.plain: Starter disable circuit reads stuck low — short to ground or low-side driver stuck on. The starter is permanently disabled, blocking engine cranking.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P081B.title: Starter Disable Circuit High
P081B.plain: Starter disable circuit reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. The disable cannot be asserted, weakening the safety chain.
causes: Disable wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P081C.title: Park Input Circuit
P081C.plain: General electrical fault on the Park input circuit — used by ECM/PCM to know that the gear lever is in Park (allows engine start, raises idle for accessory loads). With the input invalid Park-conditional logic falls back to a safe default.
causes: Open or shorted park input wire

P081D.title: Neutral Input Circuit
P081D.plain: General electrical fault on the Neutral input circuit — used by ECM/PCM to detect Neutral and adjust idle speed and start enable.
causes: Open or shorted neutral input wire

P081E.title: Excessive Clutch B Slippage
P081E.plain: Same condition as excessive clutch A slippage, applied to clutch B (second clutch in dual-clutch boxes — the odd-gear clutch typically).

P081F.title: Brake Transmission Shift Interlock (BTSI) Signal Correlation
P081F.plain: The Brake Transmission Shift Interlock prevents shifting out of Park unless the brake pedal is pressed. The TCM compares the brake-pedal input to the BTSI solenoid command and detects an inconsistency — for example shift permitted while brake not pressed, or interlock active while brake is pressed.

P0820.title: Gear Lever X-Y Position Sensor Circuit
P0820.plain: The TCM detects an out-of-range or implausible signal from the gear lever X-Y position sensor used on shift-by-wire transmissions.

P0821.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit
P0821.plain: General electrical fault on the X-axis (left/right) position sensor 1 of an electronic gear lever. Used in stick-shift-by-wire systems where the lever is decoded into X/Y coordinates rather than discrete switches.

P0822.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit
P0822.plain: General electrical fault on the Y-axis (forward/backward) position sensor 1 of an electronic gear lever.

P0823.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0823.plain: Gear lever X position sensor 1 signal jumps or drops out — typically a worn rotary contact or vibration on the centre console.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0824.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P0824.plain: Gear lever Y position sensor 1 signal jumps or drops out. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector with intermittent contact under vibration

P0825.title: Gear Lever Push-Pull Switch (Shift Anticipate)
P0825.plain: General electrical fault on the gear-lever push-pull switch — a low-force capacitive or microswitch sensor in the lever knob that detects the operator gripping the lever before it actually moves. Used for shift-anticipation, where the TCM can pre-charge a friction element so the upcoming shift feels seamless.

P0826.title: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit
P0826.plain: The TCM detects a fault in the combined up/down shift switch circuit, where both switch states are simultaneously active or both inactive when activity is expected.

P0827.title: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit Low
P0827.plain: Up/down shift switch input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-pressed paddle/button. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0828.title: Up and Down Shift Switch Circuit High
P0828.plain: Up/down shift switch input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0829.title: 5-6 Shift
P0829.plain: General fault detected during the 5-to-6 upshift event.

P082A.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Range/Performance
P082A.plain: Gear lever X sensor 1 is electrically intact, but its readings drift outside the calibrated range or do not match the redundant sensor 2.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P082B.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit Low
P082B.plain: Gear lever X sensor 1 reads stuck low — short to ground or open reference. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P082C.title: Gear Lever X Position Sensor 1 Circuit High
P082C.plain: Gear lever X sensor 1 reads stuck high — short to reference voltage or open signal return. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P082D.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit Range/Performance
P082D.plain: Gear lever Y sensor 1 is electrically intact, but its readings drift outside the calibrated range. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Sensor element aged beyond calibration window

P082E.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit Low
P082E.plain: Gear lever Y sensor 1 reads stuck low — short to ground. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P082F.title: Gear Lever Y Position Sensor 1 Circuit High
P082F.plain: Gear lever Y sensor 1 reads stuck high — short to reference voltage. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Signal wire shorted to reference voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0830.title: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit
P0830.plain: The ECU detects an electrical fault on the clutch pedal position switch A used by manual transmission engine control for cruise, start enable and idle correction.

P0831.title: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit Low
P0831.plain: Clutch pedal switch A input reads stuck low — short to ground or stuck-closed contact. The ECM may treat clutch as constantly disengaged, blocking cruise control or affecting cranking permission on manual transmissions.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0832.title: Clutch Pedal Switch A Circuit High
P0832.plain: Clutch pedal switch A input reads stuck high — short to battery voltage. Cannot detect when clutch is pressed.
causes: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0833.title: Clutch Pedal Switch B Circuit
P0833.plain: General electrical fault on the second clutch pedal switch B — provides redundant clutch-state detection (one switch upper end of pedal travel, other lower end) so the ECM can verify both ends of pedal motion. Used for accurate cranking and cruise enable logic.

P0834.title: Clutch Pedal Switch B Circuit Low
P0834.plain: Clutch pedal switch B input reads stuck low. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance

P0835.title: Clutch Pedal Switch B Circuit High
P0835.plain: Clutch pedal switch B input reads stuck high. Wiring faults of this kind typically come from chafing, water ingress at connector seals, or pin push-back — a wiggle test on the harness while the code is active often confirms the location.
causes: Switch wire shorted to battery voltage
Connector pins corroded - high contact resistance
Supply wire pinched against B+ source

P0836.title: Four Wheel Drive (4WD) Switch Circuit

P0A7D.title: Hybrid Battery Pack Low Voltage

P0A7E.title: Hybrid Battery Pack Overtemperature
P0A7E.plain: BMS detects HV pack temperature above the safe operating limit, triggering thermal protection mode and limiting charge/discharge.

P0A7F.title: Hybrid Battery Pack Deterioration
P0A7F.plain: The hybrid battery pack capacity or internal resistance has degraded beyond the diagnostic threshold. Performance and fuel economy fall as the pack ages.

P0A80.title: Replace Hybrid Battery Pack
